title.zh: 卷108之一 禮志四之一
title.raw: 卷108之一 禮志四之一 Volume 108a Treatise 4: Rituals 1

sentences.zh: 夫在天莫明於日月，在人莫明於禮儀。

translations.literal: Among things in Heaven, nothing is brighter than the sun and moon; among things in humanity, nothing is brighter than ritual and propriety.
translations.idiomatic: In Heaven nothing shines more clearly than the sun and moon; in human affairs nothing shines more clearly than ritual and propriety.

sentences.zh: 先王以安上治民，用成風化，苟或失之，斯亡云及。

translations.literal: Former kings used them to settle those above and govern the people, thereby accomplishing transformation by teaching; if one should lose them, destruction is at hand.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings employed ritual to secure those above and govern the people below, thereby shaping custom and moral influence; once it is lost, ruin follows swiftly.

sentences.zh: 聖者因人有尊敬哀思嗜慾喜怒之情，而制以上下隆殺長幼眾寡之節，本於人心，會於神道，故使三才惟穆，百姓允諧。

translations.literal: The sages, because people have feelings of respect, mourning, longing, desire, joy, and anger, fashioned regulations of elevation and diminution, senior and junior, many and few—rooted in the human heart and joined with the way of the spirits, thus making the three powers harmonious and the hundred clans concordant.
translations.idiomatic: The sages took human feelings—reverence, grief, longing, appetite, joy, and anger—and on that basis set gradations of rank, precedence, age, and number. Grounded in the human heart and aligned with the spirit world, they brought the three realms into harmony and made the people live in accord.

sentences.zh: 而淳澆世殊，質文異設，損益相仍，隨時作範。

translations.literal: Yet purity and decadence differ by age, substance and ornament are set differently, decrease and increase follow one another, and standards are fashioned according to the times.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ages differ in refinement and decline; substance and ornament take different forms; ritual is trimmed or enlarged in succession, and each age fashions its own model.

sentences.zh: 秦滅儒經，漢承其弊，三代之禮，蓋如綫焉。

translations.literal: Qin destroyed the Confucian classics; Han inherited its harm; the rituals of the Three Dynasties hung by a thread.
translations.idiomatic: Qin annihilated the Confucian canon; Han inherited the wreckage; the rituals of the Three Dynasties survived only as a thread.

sentences.zh: 劉氏中興，頗率周典，魏晉之世，抑有可知。

translations.literal: When the Liu house revived, they largely followed Zhou institutions; in the Wei and Jin age, something could still be known.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han house revived the realm, it largely followed Zhou models; under Wei and Jin, something of ritual could still be discerned.

sentences.zh: 自永嘉擾攘，神州蕪穢，禮壞樂崩，人神殲殄。

translations.literal: From the turmoil of the Yongjia era, the divine land lay waste; ritual was ruined and music collapsed; humans and spirits were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongjia upheavals, the heartland was laid waste; ritual broke down and music fell apart; both the living and the sacred were blighted.

sentences.zh: 太祖南定燕趙，日不暇給，仍世征伐，務恢疆宇。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizu pacified Yan and Zhao in the south; day after day he had no leisure; generation after generation he waged campaigns, striving to recover territory.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizu subdued Yan and Zhao in the south; day after day he had no leisure, campaigning through successive reigns to recover lost dominions.

sentences.zh: 雖馬上治之，未遑制作，至於經國軌儀，互舉其大，但事多粗略，且兼闕遺。

translations.literal: Although he governed from horseback, he had no leisure to establish institutions; as for the great norms of governing the state, he touched on them in turn, but affairs were mostly crude and many were also left out.
translations.idiomatic: Though he ruled from the saddle, he had no time to codify institutions; on the great frameworks of statecraft he took only the outlines, and much remained rough or incomplete.

sentences.zh: 高祖稽古，率由舊則，斟酌前王，擇其令典，朝章國範，煥乎復振。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu examined antiquity, followed the old rules, weighed the former kings and selected their excellent norms; court regulations and national models gleamed and revived.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu looked to antiquity, followed established precedent, weighed the practices of earlier rulers and chose the best models—and court ritual and national norms shone forth anew.

sentences.zh: 早年厭世，叡慮未從，不爾劉馬之迹，夫何足數。

translations.literal: He died young of the world; his lofty designs were not carried out—otherwise how could the traces of Liu and Ma alone be worth counting?
translations.idiomatic: He died young before his plans ripened; had he lived, how could the achievements of Liu and Ma alone have defined the age?

sentences.zh: 世宗優遊在上，致意玄門，儒業文風，顧有未洽，墜禮淪聲，因之而往。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong idled above and turned his mind to the arcane schools; Confucian learning and literary custom were not fully harmonized; fallen ritual and lost music thereby went on.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong dallied on the throne, favoring esoteric teachings; Confucian learning and literary culture never fully took root, and ritual and music continued to slip away.

sentences.zh: 肅宗已降，魏道衰羸，太和之風，仍世凋落，以至於海內傾圮，綱紀泯然。

translations.literal: From Emperor Suzong onward, Wei's Way weakened; the wind of Taihe withered reign after reign, until within the seas all was thrown down and pillars and cords were extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Suzong on, the Wei way declined; the spirit of Taihe withered reign after reign, until the realm collapsed and order vanished utterly.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 魯秉周禮，國以克固；

translations.literal: Lu held to Zhou ritual, and the state was thereby able to stand firm;
translations.idiomatic: Lu clung to Zhou ritual, and the state held firm;

sentences.zh: 齊臣撤器，降人折謀。

translations.literal: A minister of Qi removed the vessels, and the surrendering man broke his plot.
translations.idiomatic: When a Qi minister removed the ritual vessels, an enemy's plot was undone at once.

sentences.zh: 治身不得以造次忘，治國庸可而須臾忽也。

translations.literal: In ordering the body one may not forget ritual even in haste; how could ordering the state be neglected even for a moment?
translations.idiomatic: In self-cultivation one must never set ritual aside even in haste; in governing a state, how could one neglect it even for a moment?

sentences.zh: 初自皇始，迄於武定，朝廷典禮之迹，故總而錄之。

translations.literal: From the beginning at Huangshi through to Wuding, traces of court ritual are therefore gathered and recorded as a whole.
translations.idiomatic: From the Huangshi era through Wuding, the court's ritual record is gathered here as a whole.

sentences.zh: 太祖登國元年，即代王位於牛川，西向設祭，告天成禮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Daizu's ascent of the state, he took the throne of Dai at Niuchuan, set up sacrifice facing west, and performed the rite of announcing to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the founding of the state, Emperor Daizu assumed the throne of Dai at Niuchuan, offered sacrifice facing west, and performed the rite of announcing his reign to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 天興元年，定都平城，即皇帝位，立壇兆告祭天地。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxing, he fixed the capital at Pingcheng, took the imperial throne, and established altar sites to announce sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianxing he made Pingcheng his capital, ascended the imperial throne, and established altars to report his accession to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 祝曰：「皇帝臣珪敢用玄牡，昭告于皇天后土之靈。

translations.literal: The prayer said: "The emperor, your subject Gui, dares to use a black bull, clearly announcing to the spirits of August Heaven and August Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer ran: "The emperor, your subject Gui, dares to offer a black bull and plainly declare this to the spirits of August Heaven and August Earth.

sentences.zh: 上天降命，乃眷我祖宗世王幽都。

translations.literal: August Heaven sent down the mandate, cherishing our forefathers who for generations ruled Youdu.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sent down the mandate and favored our ancestors, who for generations ruled Youdu.

sentences.zh: 珪以不德，纂戎前緒，思寧黎元，龔行天罰。

translations.literal: Gui, lacking in virtue, succeeded to the martial enterprise of our predecessors, thinking to pacify the black-haired people, and reverently to execute Heaven's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Gui, lacking in virtue, took up the martial legacy of our forebears, sought to bring peace to the people, and reverently carried out Heaven's punishment.

sentences.zh: 殪劉顯，屠衞辰，平慕容，定中夏。

translations.literal: I destroyed Liu Xian, slaughtered Wei Chen, pacified Murong, and settled the Central Lands.
translations.idiomatic: I destroyed Liu Xian, overthrew Wei Chen, pacified Murong, and settled the Central Lands.

sentences.zh: 羣下勸進，謂宜正位居尊，以副天人之望。

translations.literal: The multitude below urged advancement, saying I should properly occupy the lofty position to match the expectation of Heaven and men.
translations.idiomatic: My subjects urged me to advance, saying I ought to take the supreme place to fulfill the hopes of Heaven and humanity.

sentences.zh: 珪以天時人謀，不可久替，謹命禮官，擇吉日受皇帝璽綬。

translations.literal: Gui, because Heaven's seasons and men's counsel could not long be rejected, respectfully ordered the ritual officers to choose an auspicious day to receive the imperial seal and ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Gui, because Heaven's time and human counsel could no longer be refused, respectfully ordered the ritual officers to choose an auspicious day to receive the imperial seal and cord.

sentences.zh: 惟神祇其丕祚於魏室，永綏四方。」

translations.literal: May the spirits and gods grandly bless the house of Wei and forever pacify the four quarters."
translations.idiomatic: May the spirits grandly bless the house of Wei and forever bring peace to the four quarters."

sentences.zh: 事畢，詔有司定行次，正服色。

translations.literal: When the affair was done, he issued an edict the responsible offices to fix the order of movements and rectify dress colors.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was finished, he ordered the responsible offices to fix ceremonial precedence and regulate court dress and colors.

sentences.zh: 羣臣奏以國家繼黃帝之後，宜為土德，故神獸如牛，牛土畜，又黃星顯曜，其符也。

translations.literal: The ministers memorialized that the state followed after the Yellow Emperor and ought to take Earth Virtue; therefore divine beasts were like oxen—oxen are Earth animals—and moreover the Yellow Star appeared bright, its omen.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers argued that the state succeeded the Yellow Emperor and should adopt the virtue of Earth; divine beasts therefore appeared as oxen, for the ox is the animal of Earth, and the Yellow Star shone forth as its sign.

sentences.zh: 於是始從土德，數用五，服尚黃，犧牲用白。

translations.literal: Thereupon they first followed Earth Virtue, numbers used five, dress prized yellow, and sacrifices used white.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they adopted Earth Virtue: the number five governed ritual reckoning, yellow was honored in dress, and white victims were used in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 祀天之禮用周典，以夏四月親祀于西郊，徽幟有加焉。

translations.literal: The ritual of sacrificing to Heaven used Zhou canon; in the fourth month of summer he personally sacrificed at the Western Suburb, with insignia and banners augmented.
translations.idiomatic: The rite of sacrificing to Heaven followed Zhou usage; in the fourth month of summer the emperor personally sacrificed at the Western Suburb, with added banners and insignia.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，帝親祀上帝于南郊，以始祖神元皇帝配。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, the emperor personally sacrificed to the Supreme God at the Southern Suburb, with the Founding Ancestor Emperor Shenyuan as assessor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year the emperor personally sacrificed to the Supreme God at the Southern Suburb, with the founding ancestor Emperor Shenyuan as co-honoree.

sentences.zh: 為壇通四陛，為壝埒三重。

translations.literal: They made an altar with four ramps connecting it, and an embankment and ridge threefold.
translations.idiomatic: They built an altar with four ramps and a triple embankment and ridge.

sentences.zh: 天位在其上，南面，神元西面。

translations.literal: The Heaven seat was above it, facing south; Shenyuan faced west.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's place stood above, facing south; Shenyuan faced west.

sentences.zh: 五精帝在壇內，壝內四帝，各於其方，一帝在未。

translations.literal: The Five Essence Emperors were within the altar; within the embankment were the four emperors, each in his direction, with one emperor at Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Essence Emperors stood within the altar; within the embankment the four directional emperors each occupied his quarter, with one emperor placed at Wei.

sentences.zh: 日月五星、二十八宿、天一、太一、北斗、司中、司命、司祿、司民在中壝內，各因其方。

translations.literal: The sun, moon, five stars, twenty-eight lodges, Tianyi, Taiyi, the Northern Dipper, Director of the Center, Director of Fate, Director of Salary, and Director of the People were within the middle embankment, each according to his direction.
translations.idiomatic: The sun and moon, the five planets, the twenty-eight lodges, Tianyi, Taiyi, the Northern Dipper, and the directors of the center, fate, salary, and people were placed within the middle embankment, each in its proper direction.

sentences.zh: 其餘從食者合一千餘神，餟在外壝內。

translations.literal: The rest who shared the food, together more than a thousand spirits, received libation within the outer embankment.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand lesser spirits who shared in the offering received libation within the outer embankment.

sentences.zh: 藉用藁秸，玉用四珪，幣用束帛，牲用黝犢，[1]器用陶匏。

translations.literal: Mats used straw stalks, jade used four gui, silks used bundled cloth, victims used dark calves,[1] and vessels used pottery and gourds.
translations.idiomatic: Straw mats were used for seating, four gui tablets for jade, bundled silks for offerings, dark calves for victims,[1] and pottery and gourd vessels for the rite.

sentences.zh: 上帝、神元用犢各一，五方帝共用犢一，日月等共用牛一。

translations.literal: The Supreme God and Shenyuan each used one calf; the Five Direction Emperors together used one calf; the sun, moon, and the like together used one ox.
translations.idiomatic: The Supreme God and Shenyuan each received one calf; the Five Directional Emperors shared one calf; the sun, moon, and the rest shared one ox.

sentences.zh: 祭畢，燎牲體左於壇南巳地，從陽之義。

translations.literal: When the sacrifice was done, they burned the left portion of the victim's body at the si position south of the altar, following the yang principle.
translations.idiomatic: When the sacrifice was finished, the left portion of the victim was burned at the si position south of the altar, in accord with the principle of yang.

sentences.zh: 其瘞地壇兆，制同南郊。

translations.literal: The buried-earth altar site was made the same as the Southern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: The altar for burying offerings to Earth was built on the same plan as the Southern Suburb.

sentences.zh: 明年正月辛酉，郊天。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year, on xinyou, suburban sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year, on the day xinyou, they performed the suburban sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，瘞地於北郊，以神元竇皇后配。

translations.literal: On guihai, buried-earth at the Northern Suburb, with Empress Dowager Dou of Shenyuan as assessor.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai they buried offerings to Earth at the Northern Suburb, with Empress Dowager Dou of Shenyuan as co-honoree.

sentences.zh: 五岳名山在中壝內，四瀆大川於外壝內。

translations.literal: The Five Peaks and famous mountains were within the middle embankment; the four streams and great rivers were within the outer embankment.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Sacred Peaks and famous mountains stood within the middle embankment; the four rivers and great waterways within the outer embankment.

sentences.zh: 后土、神元后，牲共用玄牡一，[2]玉用兩珪，幣用束帛，五岳等用牛一。

translations.literal: Hou Tu and the Shenyuan empress together used one black bull,[2] jade used two gui, silks used bundled cloth, and the Five Peaks and the like each used one ox.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Tu and the Shenyuan empress shared one black bull;[2] two gui tablets were used for jade, bundled silks for offerings, and the Five Peaks and the like each received one ox.

sentences.zh: 祭畢，瘞牲體右於壇之北亥地，從陰也。

translations.literal: When the sacrifice was done, they buried the right portion of the victim's body at the hai position north of the altar, following yin.
translations.idiomatic: When the sacrifice was finished, the right portion of the victim was buried at the hai position north of the altar, in accord with yin.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，赦京師畿內五歲刑以下。

translations.literal: On yichou, amnesty within the capital precinct for punishments of five years or less.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou he granted amnesty within the capital region to those sentenced to five years or less.

sentences.zh: 其後，冬至祭上帝于圓丘，夏至祭地于方澤，用牲幣之屬，與二郊同。

translations.literal: Thereafter, at the winter solstice they sacrificed to the Supreme God at the round mound; at the summer solstice they sacrificed to Earth at the square marsh; victims, silks, and the like were the same as at the two suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, at the winter solstice they sacrificed to the Supreme God at the round mound; at the summer solstice they sacrificed to Earth at the square marsh; victims, silks, and the like matched those used at the two suburban rites.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，平文、昭成、獻明廟成。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, the temples of Pingwen, Zhaocheng, and Xianming were completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter the temples of Pingwen, Zhaocheng, and Xianming were completed.

sentences.zh: 歲五祭，用二至、二分、臘，牲用太牢，常遣宗正兼太尉率祀官侍祀。

translations.literal: Five sacrifices per year, using the two solstices, two equinoxes, and year-end; victims used the great pen; routinely the Director of the Imperial Clan concurrently serving as Grand Commandant led sacrificial officers to attend the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: They were sacrificed to five times a year, at the two solstices, the two equinoxes, and the year-end festival, with the great pen; the Director of the Imperial Clan, also serving as Grand Commandant, regularly led the sacrificial officers.

sentences.zh: 置太社、太稷、帝社於宗廟之右，為方壇四陛。

translations.literal: They set Great Soil, Great Millet, and Imperial Soil to the right of the ancestral temple, as a square altar with four ramps.
translations.idiomatic: Great Soil, Great Millet, and Imperial Soil were placed to the right of the ancestral temple, each on a square altar with four ramps.

sentences.zh: 祀以二月、八月，用戊，皆太牢。

translations.literal: They were sacrificed to in the second and eighth months, on wu days, all with the great pen.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice was performed in the second and eighth months on wu days, always with the great pen.

sentences.zh: 句龍配社，周棄配稷，皆有司侍祀。

translations.literal: Goulong was assessor for the soil altar, Hou Ji for the millet altar; all had officials attending sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Goulong was paired with the soil altar and Hou Ji with the millet altar; in each case officials attended the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 立祖神，常以正月上未，設藉於端門內，祭牲用羊、豕、犬各一。

translations.literal: They established the Ancestor Spirit; regularly on the upper wei day of the first month they set mats inside the Front Gate, and sacrifice victims used one sheep, one pig, and one dog each.
translations.idiomatic: They established the Ancestor Spirit; on the upper wei day of the first month mats were laid inside the Front Gate, and one sheep, one pig, and one dog were offered.

sentences.zh: 又立神元、思帝、平文、昭成、獻明五帝廟於宮中，歲四祭，用正、冬、臘、九月，牲用馬、牛各一，太祖親祀宮中。

translations.literal: They also established temples to the five emperors Shenyuan, Sidi, Pingwen, Zhaocheng, and Xianming within the palace; four sacrifices per year in the first month, winter, year-end, and ninth month; victims used one horse and one ox each; Emperor Daizu personally sacrificed within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Temples to the five emperors Shenyuan, Sidi, Pingwen, Zhaocheng, and Xianming were also built within the palace; they were sacrificed to four times a year in the first month, winter, year-end, and ninth month, with one horse and one ox each; Emperor Daizu personally performed the rites within the palace.

sentences.zh: 立星神，一歲一祭，常以十二月，用馬薦各一，[3]牛豕各二，雞一。

translations.literal: They established the Star Spirit; one sacrifice per year, regularly in the twelfth month, using one horse offering each,[3] two oxen and two pigs each, and one chicken.
translations.idiomatic: They established the Star Spirit, sacrificed to once a year, usually in the twelfth month, with one horse offering,[3] two oxen, two pigs, and one chicken.

sentences.zh: 太祖初，有兩彗星見，劉后使占者占之，曰：「祈之則當掃定天下。」

translations.literal: In Emperor Daizu's early days, two comets appeared; Empress Liu had diviners divine them, who said: "If you pray to them, you will sweep and settle the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Daizu's reign two comets appeared; Empress Liu had diviners interpret them, who said, "If you pray to them, you will sweep the realm clean and bring it to order."

sentences.zh: 后從之，故立其祀。

translations.literal: The empress followed this, therefore they established their cult.
translations.idiomatic: The empress followed their advice, and so the cult was established.

sentences.zh: 又立□□神十二，歲一祭，常以十一月，各用牛一、雞三。

translations.literal: They also established twelve □□ spirits; one sacrifice per year, regularly in the eleventh month, each using one ox and three chickens.
translations.idiomatic: They also established twelve spirits whose names are lost in the text; they were sacrificed to once a year, usually in the eleventh month, each with one ox and three chickens.

sentences.zh: 又立王神四，歲二祭，常以八月、十月，各用羊一。

translations.literal: They also established four King Spirits; two sacrifices per year, regularly in the eighth and tenth months, each using one sheep.
translations.idiomatic: They also established four King Spirits, sacrificed to twice a year, usually in the eighth and tenth months, each with one sheep.

sentences.zh: 又置獻明以上所立天神四十所，歲二祭，亦以八月、十月。

translations.literal: They also set up forty heaven-spirit sites established from Xianming upward; two sacrifices per year, also in the eighth and tenth months.
translations.idiomatic: They also maintained forty heaven-spirit shrines established from Xianming's time onward, sacrificed to twice a year, likewise in the eighth and tenth months.

sentences.zh: 神尊者以馬，次以牛，小以羊，皆女巫行事。

translations.literal: For the most honored spirits they used horses, next oxen, for lesser ones sheep; all were conducted by shamanesses.
translations.idiomatic: The highest-ranked spirits received horses, the next oxen, and lesser ones sheep; shamanesses performed all these rites.

sentences.zh: 又於雲中及盛樂神元舊都祀神元以下七帝，歲三祭，正、冬、臘，用馬牛各一，祀官侍祀。

translations.literal: Also at Yunzhong and at Shenyuan's old capital at Shengle they sacrificed to the seven emperors from Shenyuan down; three sacrifices per year in the first month, winter, and year-end; they used one horse and one ox each; sacrificial officers attended.
translations.idiomatic: At Yunzhong and at Shenyuan's old capital of Shengle they also sacrificed to the seven emperors from Shenyuan downward, three times a year in the first month, winter, and year-end, with one horse and one ox each, attended by sacrificial officers.

sentences.zh: 明年春，帝始躬耕籍田，祭先農，用羊一。

translations.literal: The next spring, the emperor first personally plowed the sacred field, sacrificed to the First Farmer, using one sheep.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring the emperor first personally plowed the sacred field and sacrificed to the First Farmer with one sheep.

sentences.zh: 祀日於東郊，用騂牛一。

translations.literal: They sacrificed to the sun at the Eastern Suburb, using one red bull.
translations.idiomatic: The sun was sacrificed to at the Eastern Suburb with one red bull.

sentences.zh: 秋分祭月於西郊，用白羊一。

translations.literal: At the autumn equinox they sacrificed to the moon at the Western Suburb, using one white sheep.
translations.idiomatic: At the autumn equinox the moon was sacrificed to at the Western Suburb with one white sheep.

sentences.zh: 天賜二年夏四月，復祀天于西郊，為方壇一，置木主七於上。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer in the second year of Tianci, they again sacrificed to Heaven at the Western Suburb, made one square altar, and placed seven wooden tablets on it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer in the second year of Tianci they again sacrificed to Heaven at the Western Suburb, building a single square altar with seven wooden spirit tablets upon it.

sentences.zh: 東為二陛，無等；

translations.literal: On the east were two ramps, without gradation;
translations.idiomatic: On the east side were two ramps, without graded steps;

sentences.zh: 周垣四門，門各依其方色為名。

translations.literal: The perimeter wall had four gates, each gate named according to its directional color.
translations.idiomatic: The enclosing wall had four gates, each named for the color of its direction.

sentences.zh: 牲用白犢、黃駒、白羊各一。

translations.literal: Victims used one white calf, one yellow colt, and one white sheep each.
translations.idiomatic: The victims were one white calf, one yellow colt, and one white sheep.

sentences.zh: 祭之日，帝御大駕，百官及賓國諸部大人畢從至郊所。

translations.literal: On the day of sacrifice, the emperor rode the great carriage; all officials and chieftains of guest states and various tribes fully followed to the suburban site.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of sacrifice the emperor rode in the great carriage, and all officials and chieftains of tributary states and tribal confederations followed in full array to the suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 帝立青門內近南壇西，內朝臣皆位於帝北，外朝臣及大人咸位於青門之外，后率六宮從黑門入，列於青門內近北，並西面。

translations.literal: The emperor stood inside the Green Gate near the west of the southern altar; inner court officials were all north of the emperor; outer court officials and chieftains were all outside the Green Gate; the empress led the six palaces in through the Black Gate and lined up inside the Green Gate near the north, all facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stood inside the Green Gate near the west side of the southern altar; inner-court officials took their places north of him; outer-court officials and tribal chieftains stood outside the Green Gate; the empress led the six palaces in through the Black Gate and lined up inside the Green Gate toward the north, all facing west.

sentences.zh: 廩犧令掌牲，陳於壇前。

translations.literal: The Director of the Granary Victims managed the victims and displayed them before the altar.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Sacrificial Victims supervised the offerings and set them out before the altar.

sentences.zh: 女巫執鼓，立於陛之東，西面。

translations.literal: A shamaness held the drum, standing east of the ramp, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: A shamaness held the drum and stood east of the ramp, facing west.

sentences.zh: 選帝之十族子弟七人執酒，在巫南，西面北上。

translations.literal: Seven youths chosen from the ten clans of the emperor's kin held wine, south of the shamaness, facing west and ascending northward.
translations.idiomatic: Seven youths chosen from the emperor's ten clans held wine south of the shamaness, facing west and arranged from south to north.

sentences.zh: 女巫升壇，搖鼓。

translations.literal: The shamaness ascended the altar and shook the drum.
translations.idiomatic: The shamaness ascended the altar and beat the drum.

sentences.zh: 帝拜，后肅拜，[4]百官內外盡拜。

translations.literal: The emperor bowed, the empress performed a respectful bow,[4] and all officials within and without bowed fully.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed, the empress performed a respectful bow,[4] and all officials inside and outside the gate bowed in turn.

sentences.zh: 祀訖，復拜。

translations.literal: When the sacrifice was done, they bowed again.
translations.idiomatic: When the offering was finished, they bowed again.

sentences.zh: 拜訖，乃殺牲。

translations.literal: When the bowing was done, then they slaughtered the victims.
translations.idiomatic: After the bows were completed, the victims were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 執酒七人西向，以酒灑天神主，復拜，如此者七。

translations.literal: The seven who held wine faced west, sprinkled wine on the heaven-god tablets, bowed again, and did so seven times.
translations.idiomatic: The seven wine-bearers faced west, sprinkled wine on the heaven-god tablets, bowed again, and repeated this seven times.

sentences.zh: 禮畢而返。

translations.literal: When the ritual was done, they returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was finished, they returned.

sentences.zh: 自是之後，歲一祭。

translations.literal: From this time onward, one sacrifice per year.
translations.idiomatic: From then on it was performed once a year.

sentences.zh: 太宗永興三年三月，帝禱于武周車輪二山。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Yongxing of Emperor Taizong, the emperor prayed at the two mountains of Wuzhou and Chelun.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year of Yongxing, Emperor Taizong prayed at Mount Wuzhou and Mount Chelun.

sentences.zh: 初清河王紹有寵於太祖，性凶悍，帝每以義責之，弗從。

translations.literal: Earlier Prince Qinghe Shao had been favored by Emperor Daizu; his nature was fierce and violent; the emperor often reproved him with righteousness, but he would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Prince Qinghe Shao had enjoyed Emperor Daizu's favor, but his nature was fierce and violent; the emperor often rebuked him on grounds of right conduct, yet he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 帝懼其變，乃於山上祈福於天地神祇。

translations.literal: The emperor feared his rebellion, and therefore on the mountain prayed for blessing to the spirits of Heaven, Earth, and the gods.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a coup, the emperor prayed on the mountain for blessing from the spirits of Heaven, Earth, and the gods.

sentences.zh: 及即位壇兆，後因以為常祀，歲一祭，牲用牛，帝皆親之，無常日。

translations.literal: When he took the throne he established altar sites; afterward this became a regular sacrifice, one per year, victims using an ox; the emperor always performed it personally, without a fixed day.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne he established altars there; later this became a regular annual sacrifice with an ox, which the emperor always performed in person on no fixed calendar day.

sentences.zh: 明年，立太祖廟于白登山。

translations.literal: The next year, they established Emperor Daizu's temple on Mount Baideng.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they built Emperor Daizu's temple on Mount Baideng.

sentences.zh: 歲一祭，具太牢，帝親之，亦無常月。

translations.literal: One sacrifice per year, fully furnished with the great pen; the emperor performed it personally, also without a fixed month.
translations.idiomatic: It was sacrificed to once a year with the full great pen; the emperor performed the rite in person, likewise on no fixed month.

sentences.zh: 兼祀皇天上帝，以山神配，旱則禱之，多有效。

translations.literal: They also sacrificed to August Heaven and the Supreme God, with the mountain spirit as assessor; in drought they prayed there, and it was often effective.
translations.idiomatic: August Heaven and the Supreme God were also worshiped there, with the mountain spirit as co-honoree; in drought they prayed at this shrine, and it often proved effective.

sentences.zh: 是歲，詔郡國於太祖巡幸行宮之所，各立壇，祭以太牢，歲一祭，皆牧守侍祀。

translations.literal: That year, he issued an edict the commanderies and kingdoms that at each place where Emperor Daizu had toured and had traveling palaces, they should each establish an altar, sacrifice with the great pen, one sacrifice per year, all with governors and defenders attending sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: That year he ordered every commandery and kingdom to erect an altar wherever Emperor Daizu had toured or had a traveling palace, to sacrifice with the great pen once a year, with local governors and defenders officiating.

sentences.zh: 又立太祖別廟於宮中，歲四祭，用牛馬羊各一。

translations.literal: They also established a separate temple to Emperor Daizu within the palace; four sacrifices per year, using one ox, one horse, and one sheep each.
translations.idiomatic: A separate temple to Emperor Daizu was also built within the palace, sacrificed to four times a year with one ox, one horse, and one sheep.

sentences.zh: 又加置天日月之神及諸小神二十八所於宮內，歲二祭，各用羊一。

translations.literal: They also added shrines to the spirits of Heaven, sun, moon, and twenty-eight lesser spirits within the palace; two sacrifices per year, each using one sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Shrines to the spirits of Heaven, the sun, the moon, and twenty-eight lesser deities were also set up within the palace, sacrificed to twice a year, each with one sheep.

sentences.zh: 後二年，於白登西，太祖舊遊之處，立昭成、獻明、太祖廟，常以九月、十月之交，帝親祭，牲用馬、牛、羊，及親行貙劉之禮。

translations.literal: Two years later, west of Baideng at the place where Emperor Daizu had formerly traveled, they established temples to Zhaocheng, Xianming, and Emperor Daizu; regularly at the junction of the ninth and tenth months the emperor personally sacrificed, victims using horse, ox, and sheep, and personally performed the bear-and-deer ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, west of Baideng where Emperor Daizu had once traveled, temples to Zhaocheng, Xianming, and Emperor Daizu were built; at the turn of the ninth and tenth months the emperor personally sacrificed with horse, ox, and sheep, and personally performed the bear-hunt rite.

sentences.zh: 別置天神等二十三於廟左右，其神大者以馬，小者以羊。

translations.literal: They separately set up twenty-three heaven-spirits and the like to the left and right of the temples; for the greater spirits they used horses, for lesser ones sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-three heaven-spirits and the like were separately placed to either side of the temples; greater spirits received horses, lesser ones sheep.

sentences.zh: 華陰公主，帝姊也，元紹之為逆，有保護功，故別立其廟於太祖廟垣後，因祭薦焉。

translations.literal: Princess Huayin was the emperor's elder sister; in Yuan Shao's rebellion she had merit in protecting him, therefore they separately established her temple behind the wall of Emperor Daizu's temple, and offered sacrifice and commendation there.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Huayin was the emperor's elder sister; in Yuan Shao's rebellion she had protected him, and so her shrine was separately built behind the wall of Emperor Daizu's temple, where offerings were made to her as well.

sentences.zh: 又於雲中、盛樂、金陵三所，各立太廟，四時祀官侍祀。

translations.literal: Also at Yunzhong, Shengle, and Jinling, three places, they each established Great Temples; in the four seasons sacrificial officers attended sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Great ancestral temples were also established at Yunzhong, Shengle, and Jinling, with sacrificial officers attending in all four seasons.

sentences.zh: 泰常三年，為五精帝兆於四郊，遠近依五行數。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taichang, they made sites for the Five Essence Emperors in the four suburbs, near and far according to the numbers of the Five Phases.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taichang altar sites for the Five Essence Emperors were established in the four suburbs, their distances set according to the numbers of the Five Phases.

sentences.zh: 各為方壇四陛，埒壝三重，通四門。

translations.literal: Each was a square altar with four ramps, embankment and ridge threefold, with four gates connecting through.
translations.idiomatic: Each was a square altar with four ramps, a triple embankment and ridge, and four communicating gates.

sentences.zh: 以太皡等及諸佐隨配。

translations.literal: They used Taihao and the like and various assessors as accompanying matches.
translations.idiomatic: Taihao and the other chief deities were honored, with their attendant spirits paired accordingly.

sentences.zh: 侑祭黃帝，常以立秋前十八日。

translations.literal: The secondary sacrifice to the Yellow Emperor was regularly held eighteen days before the Beginning of Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor was honored as assessor, usually eighteen days before the Beginning of Autumn.

sentences.zh: 餘四帝，各以四立之日。

translations.literal: The remaining four emperors, each on the day of its corresponding Beginning of Season.
translations.idiomatic: The other four emperors were each honored on the day of its corresponding Beginning of Season.

sentences.zh: 牲各用牛一，有司主之。

translations.literal: Victims each used one ox; responsible officials presided.
translations.idiomatic: Each sacrifice used one ox, with responsible officials presiding.

sentences.zh: 又六宗、靈星、風伯、雨師、司民、司祿、先農之壇，皆有別兆，祭有常日，牲用少牢。

translations.literal: Also altars to the Six Ancestors, the Bright Star, the Wind Lord, the Rain Master, the Director of the People, the Director of Blessings, and the First Farmer—each had its own site; sacrifice had fixed days; victims used the lesser pen.
translations.idiomatic: Altars to the Six Ancestors, the Bright Star, the Wind Lord, the Rain Master, the Director of the People, the Director of Blessings, and the First Farmer each had its own site, with fixed days of sacrifice and the lesser pen as victims.

sentences.zh: 立春之日，遣有司迎春於東郊，祭用酒、脯、棗、栗，無牲幣。

translations.literal: On the day of Beginning of Spring, officials were dispatched to welcome spring at the Eastern Suburb; offerings used wine, dried meat, jujubes, and chestnuts—no animal victims or silk.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of Beginning of Spring, officials were sent to welcome spring at the Eastern Suburb, offering wine, dried meat, jujubes, and chestnuts—without animal victims or silk.

sentences.zh: 又立五岳四瀆廟於桑乾水之陰，春秋遣有司祭，有牲及幣。

translations.literal: They also established temples to the Five Sacred Peaks and Four Rivers south of the Sanggan River; in spring and autumn officials were dispatched to sacrifice, with victims and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Temples to the Five Sacred Peaks and the Four Rivers were also built south of the Sanggan River; in spring and autumn officials were sent to sacrifice there with victims and silk.

sentences.zh: 四瀆唯以牲牢，準古望秩云。

translations.literal: For the Four Rivers only the full pen was used—following the ancient rule of according rank to what is gazed upon.
translations.idiomatic: For the Four Rivers only the full pen was used, in accordance with the ancient principle of ranking sacrifices by what is gazed upon from afar.

sentences.zh: 其餘山川及海若諸神在州郡者，合三百二十四所，每歲十月，遣祀官詣州鎮遍祀。

translations.literal: The remaining mountains, rivers, and sea spirits and the like located in the provinces totaled 324 sites; each tenth month sacrificial officers were sent to the prefectures and garrisons to sacrifice throughout.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining mountains, rivers, sea spirits, and other deities in the provinces totaled 324 sites; every tenth month sacrificial officers were dispatched to the prefectures and garrisons to sacrifice at them all.

sentences.zh: 有水旱災厲，則牧守各隨其界內祈謁，其祭皆用牲。

translations.literal: When there were floods, droughts, or epidemics, governors and defenders each prayed within their jurisdictions; all such sacrifices used victims.
translations.idiomatic: When flood, drought, or epidemic struck, governors and defenders each prayed within their own territories, and all such sacrifices used animal victims.

sentences.zh: 王畿內諸山川，皆列祀次祭，若有水旱則禱之。

translations.literal: Within the capital region all mountains and rivers were listed for graded secondary sacrifice; if flood or drought occurred they were prayed to.
translations.idiomatic: Within the capital region all mountains and rivers were enrolled for graded secondary sacrifice and prayed to whenever flood or drought occurred.

translations.literal: The text is deficient.
translations.idiomatic: The text is deficient.

sentences.zh: 明年八月，帝嘗於白登廟，將薦熟，有神異焉。

translations.literal: The next year, in the eighth month, the emperor made offering at the Baideng temple; as he was about to present the cooked sacrifice, there was a divine manifestation.
translations.idiomatic: The following August the emperor made offering at the Baideng temple; as he was about to present the cooked sacrifice, a divine manifestation occurred.

sentences.zh: 太廟博士許鍾上言曰：「臣聞聖人能饗帝，孝子能饗親。

translations.literal: Erudite of the Great Temple Xu Zhong submitted a memorial, saying: "I have heard that sages can make the Lord on High partake, and filial sons can make their parents partake.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhong, Erudite of the Great Temple, submitted a memorial: "I have heard that sages can make the Lord on High partake of their offerings, and filial sons can make their parents partake.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下孝誠之至，通於神明。

translations.literal: Humbly considering it, Your Majesty's filial sincerity reaches its utmost and communes with the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Humbly considered, Your Majesty's filial sincerity reaches its utmost and communes with the spirits.

sentences.zh: 近嘗於太祖廟，有車騎聲，從北門入，殷殷轞轞，震動門闕，執事者無不肅慄。

translations.literal: Recently, when offering at Emperor Daizu's temple, there was the sound of chariots and horsemen entering from the North Gate—rumbling and thundering, shaking the gate towers; none who were officiating failed to be awed and tremble.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, when offering at Emperor Daizu's temple, the sound of chariots and horsemen came in through the North Gate—rumbling and thundering, shaking the gate towers—so that every officiant was awed and trembling.

sentences.zh: 斯乃國祚永隆之兆，宜告天下，使咸知聖德之深遠。」

translations.literal: This is a portent that the dynastic fortune will endure forever. It is fitting to announce it to the realm, so that all may know the depth and reach of sagely virtue."
translations.idiomatic: This is a portent that the dynastic fortune will endure forever. It is fitting to announce it to the realm, so that all may know how deep and far-reaching Your Majesty's sagely virtue is."

sentences.zh: 辛未，幸代，至雁門關，望祀恒岳。

translations.literal: On xinwei, he traveled to Dai, reached Yanmen Pass, and performed distant sacrifice to Mount Heng.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinwei he traveled to Dai, reached Yanmen Pass, and performed distant sacrifice to Mount Heng.

sentences.zh: 後二年九月，幸橋山，遣有司祀黃帝、唐堯廟。

translations.literal: Two years later, in the ninth month, he visited Qiaoshan and dispatched officials to sacrifice at the temples of the Yellow Emperor and Tang Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, in the ninth month, he visited Qiaoshan and dispatched officials to sacrifice at the temples of the Yellow Emperor and Tang Yao.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，南巡恒岳，祀以太牢。

translations.literal: The next year, in the first month, he toured south to Mount Heng and sacrificed with the great pen.
translations.idiomatic: The following first month he toured south to Mount Heng and sacrificed with the great pen.

sentences.zh: 幸洛陽，[6]遣使以太牢祀嵩高、華岳。

translations.literal: At Luoyang, [6] he dispatched envoys to sacrifice to Song Gao and Mount Hua with the great pen.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang, [6] he dispatched envoys to sacrifice to Mount Song and Mount Hua with the great pen.

sentences.zh: 還登太行。

translations.literal: Returning, he ascended the Taihang Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey he ascended the Taihang Mountains.

sentences.zh: 五月，至自洛陽，諸所過山川，羣祀之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, he returned from Luoyang; all mountains and rivers passed along the way were collectively sacrificed to.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he returned from Luoyang, and all mountains and rivers along the route were sacrificed to in turn.

sentences.zh: 後三年二月，祀孔子於國學，以顏淵配。

translations.literal: Three years later, in the second month, he sacrificed to Confucius at the National Academy, with Yan Yuan as assessor.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later, in the second month, he sacrificed to Confucius at the National Academy, with Yan Yuan honored as assessor.

sentences.zh: 神䴥二年，[7]帝將征蠕蠕，省郊祀儀。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenlu, [7] as the emperor was about to campaign against the Rouran, suburban sacrifice rites were reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shenlu, [7] as the emperor was about to campaign against the Rouran, suburban sacrifice rites were simplified.

sentences.zh: 四月，以小駕祭天神，畢，帝遂親戎。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he used the lesser carriage to sacrifice to Heaven; when finished, the emperor himself took up arms.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he sacrificed to Heaven with the lesser carriage; when the rite was complete, the emperor himself took the field.

sentences.zh: 大捷而還，歸格於祖禰，徧告羣神。

translations.literal: Returning in great victory, he reported to the ancestral temples and announced to all spirits everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Returning in great victory, he reported to the ancestral temples and announced the triumph to spirits throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 九月，立密皇太后廟於鄴，后之舊鄉也。

translations.literal: In the ninth month a temple to Empress Dowager Mi was established at Ye—it was the empress's former home district.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month a temple to Empress Dowager Mi was established at Ye, her former home district.

sentences.zh: 置祀官太常博士、齋郎三十餘人，侍祀，歲五祭。

translations.literal: They appointed more than thirty sacrificial officers, Erudites of the Director of Ritual, and Fast Officers to attend sacrifice—five sacrifices per year.
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty sacrificial officers, Erudites of the Director of Ritual, and Fast Officers were appointed to attend the rites, with five sacrifices each year.

sentences.zh: 太延元年，立廟於恒岳、華岳、嵩岳上，[8]各置侍祀九十人，歲時祈禱水旱。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiyan, temples were established atop Mount Heng, Mount Hua, and Mount Song; [8] at each ninety attendants were placed, praying annually for flood or drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiyan, temples were built atop Mount Heng, Mount Hua, and Mount Song; [8] at each ninety attendants were stationed to pray throughout the year against flood and drought.

sentences.zh: 其春秋泮涸，遣官率刺史祭以牲牢，有玉幣。

translations.literal: In spring and autumn when the ice melted and rivers cleared, officials were dispatched leading prefectural governors to sacrifice with the full pen, with jade and silk.
translations.idiomatic: In spring and autumn, when the ice melted and the rivers ran clear, officials were sent leading prefectural governors to sacrifice with the full pen and jade and silk offerings.

sentences.zh: 魏先之居幽都也，鑿石為祖宗之廟於烏洛侯國西北。

translations.literal: When Wei first dwelt in Youdu, they carved stone into an ancestral temple northwest of the Wuluohou state.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei first dwelt in Youdu, they carved a stone temple to the ancestors northwest of the Wuluohou state.

sentences.zh: 自後南遷，其地隔遠。

translations.literal: Afterward, when they migrated south, the place lay far away.
translations.idiomatic: After the southward migration, the place lay far away.

sentences.zh: 真君中，烏洛侯國遣使朝獻，云石廟如故，民常祈請，有神驗焉。

translations.literal: In the Zhenjun era, the Wuluohou state sent envoys bearing tribute, reporting that the stone temple remained as before; the people constantly prayed there, and miracles were manifest.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenjun era, the Wuluohou state sent envoys bearing tribute, reporting that the stone temple remained as before; the people constantly prayed there, and miracles were manifest.

sentences.zh: 其歲，遣中書侍郎李敞詣石室，告祭天地，以皇祖先妣配。

translations.literal: That year, Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Chang was dispatched to the stone chamber to announce sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, with the imperial ancestors and consorts as assessors.
translations.idiomatic: That year Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Chang was sent to the stone chamber to announce sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, with the imperial ancestors and consorts honored as assessors.

sentences.zh: 祝曰：「天子燾謹遣敞等用駿足、一元大武敢昭告于皇天之靈。

translations.literal: The invocation said: "The Son of Heaven Tao respectfully dispatches Chang and others, using a swift horse and one great martial victim, to declare before the numinous Power of August Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The invocation ran: "The Son of Heaven Tao respectfully dispatches Chang and his party, with a swift horse and one great martial victim, to declare before the numinous Power of August Heaven.

sentences.zh: 自啟闢之初，祐我皇祖，于彼土田。

translations.literal: From the beginning when Heaven and Earth were opened, you aided our imperial ancestor in that land and fields.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Heaven and Earth were first opened, you aided our imperial ancestor in that land and fields.

sentences.zh: 歷載億年，聿來南遷。

translations.literal: Through countless years we came southward.
translations.idiomatic: Through countless years we came southward.

sentences.zh: 惟祖惟父，光宅中原。

translations.literal: Both ancestor and father gloriously dwelt in the Central Plain.
translations.idiomatic: Both ancestor and father gloriously established their dwelling in the Central Plain.

sentences.zh: 克翦凶醜，拓定四邊。

translations.literal: They cut down fierce foes and extended and settled the four borders.
translations.idiomatic: They cut down fierce enemies and extended and settled the four borders.

sentences.zh: 冲人纂業，德聲弗彰。

translations.literal: A youth inherited the enterprise; his virtue's fame was not yet displayed.
translations.idiomatic: A youth inherited the enterprise, yet his virtue's fame had not yet been displayed.

sentences.zh: 豈謂幽遐，稽首來王。

translations.literal: Who would have thought that in remote depths they would come, bowing foreheads, to pay homage.
translations.idiomatic: Who would have thought that from remote depths they would come, bowing their foreheads, to pay homage.

sentences.zh: 具知舊廟，弗毀弗亡。

translations.literal: We fully know the old temple has not been destroyed nor lost.
translations.idiomatic: We have fully learned that the old temple has neither been destroyed nor lost.

sentences.zh: 悠悠之懷，希仰餘光。

translations.literal: In deep longing we hope to look up to your remaining radiance.
translations.idiomatic: With deep longing we hope to look up to your remaining radiance.

sentences.zh: 王業之興，起自皇祖。

translations.literal: The rise of royal enterprise began from the imperial ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The rise of royal enterprise began with the imperial ancestor.

sentences.zh: 綿綿瓜瓞，時惟多祜。

translations.literal: Like spreading melons from the vine, in every season there is abundant blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Like melons spreading from the vine, in every season there is abundant blessing.

sentences.zh: 敢以丕功，配饗于天。

translations.literal: We dare with this great merit jointly partake in offering to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: We dare with this great merit to share the offering with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 子子孫孫，福祿永延。」

translations.literal: Sons and sons, grandsons and grandsons—blessings and emoluments extended forever."
translations.idiomatic: Sons upon sons, grandsons upon grandsons—may blessings and emoluments endure forever."

sentences.zh: 敞等既祭，斬樺木立之，以置牲體而還。

translations.literal: When Chang and the others had finished sacrifice, they cut birch wood and erected it, placed the victim flesh, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang and his party had finished the sacrifice, they cut birch poles, erected them, placed the victim flesh upon them, and returned.

sentences.zh: 後所立樺木生長成林，其民益神奉之。

translations.literal: Later the birch poles they had set grew into a forest; the people all the more revered them as divine.
translations.idiomatic: Later the birch poles they had erected grew into a forest, and the people revered them all the more as divine.

sentences.zh: 咸謂魏國感靈祇之應也。

translations.literal: All said it was the response of the numinous powers to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: All said it was a response of the numinous powers to Wei.

sentences.zh: 石室南距代京可四千餘里。

translations.literal: The stone chamber lay more than four thousand li south of the capital at Dai.
translations.idiomatic: The stone chamber lay more than four thousand li south of the capital at Dai.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，司徒崔浩奏議：「神祀多不經，案祀典所宜祀，凡五十七所，餘復重及小神，請皆罷之。」

translations.literal: The next year, sixth month, Minister of Works Cui Hao submitted a memorial: "Many spirit cults are unorthodox. According to the canonical register of what should be sacrificed to, there are fifty-seven in all; the rest are redundant or minor spirits—request that all be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: The following June, Minister of Works Cui Hao submitted a memorial: "Many spirit cults are unorthodox. According to the canonical register of proper sacrifices, there are fifty-seven in all; the rest are redundant or minor spirits—I request that all be abolished."

sentences.zh: 奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 十一年十一月，世祖南征，逕恒山，祀以太牢。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the eleventh year, Emperor Shizu marched south; passing Mount Heng he sacrificed with the great pen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the eleventh year, Emperor Shizu marched south; passing Mount Heng he sacrificed with the great pen.

sentences.zh: 浮河、濟，祀以少牢。

translations.literal: Crossing the Yellow River and the Ji River, he sacrificed with the lesser pen.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the Yellow River and the Ji River, he sacrificed with the lesser pen.

sentences.zh: 過岱宗，祀以太牢。

translations.literal: Passing Mount Dai, he sacrificed with the great pen.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Mount Dai, he sacrificed with the great pen.

sentences.zh: 至魯，以太牢祭孔子。

translations.literal: Arriving at Lu, he sacrificed to Confucius with the great pen.
translations.idiomatic: Arriving at Lu, he sacrificed to Confucius with the great pen.

sentences.zh: 遂臨江，登瓜步而還。

translations.literal: Then he reached the Yangzi River, ascended Guabu, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Then he reached the Yangzi River, ascended Guabu, and returned.

sentences.zh: 文成皇帝即位，二年正月，遣有司詣華岳修廟立碑。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wencheng ascended the throne, in the second month of the second year, officials were dispatched to Mount Hua to repair the temple and erect a stele.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wencheng ascended the throne, in the second month of the second year, officials were dispatched to Mount Hua to repair the temple and erect a stele.

sentences.zh: 數十人在山上，聞虛中若有音聲，聲中稱萬歲云。

translations.literal: [9] Several dozen people on the mountain heard what seemed like voices in empty air; [10] within the voices came "Long live the Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: [9] Several dozen people on the mountain heard what seemed like voices in empty air; [10] among the voices came cries of "Long live the Emperor."

sentences.zh: 和平元年正月，帝東巡。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Heping, the emperor toured east.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Heping, the emperor toured east.

sentences.zh: 歷橋山，祀黃帝；

translations.literal: Passing Qiaoshan, he sacrificed to the Yellow Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Passing Qiaoshan, he sacrificed to the Yellow Emperor;

sentences.zh: 幸遼西，望祀醫無閭山。

translations.literal: Traveling to Liaoxi, he performed distant sacrifice to Mount Yiwulu.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling to Liaoxi, he performed distant sacrifice to Mount Yiwulu.

sentences.zh: 遂緣海西南，幸冀州，北至中山，過恒岳，禮其神而返。

translations.literal: Then following the coast southwest, he visited Jizhou; north to Zhongshan, passing Mount Heng, he performed rites to its spirit and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Then following the coast southwest, he visited Jizhou; going north to Zhongshan and passing Mount Heng, he performed rites to its spirit and returned.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝南巡，過石門，遣使者用玉璧牲牢，禮恒岳。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor toured south; passing Shimen, he dispatched envoys to perform rites at Mount Heng with jade disks and the full pen.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor toured south; passing Shimen, he dispatched envoys to perform rites at Mount Heng with jade disks and the full pen.

sentences.zh: 四月旱，下詔州郡，於其界內神無大小，悉洒掃薦以酒脯。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, drought; an edict went to the provinces and commanderies that within their borders, spirits great and small, all were to be swept clean and offered wine and dried meat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month there was drought; an edict went to the provinces and commanderies that within their borders, spirits great and small, were all to be swept clean and offered wine and dried meat.

sentences.zh: 年登之後，各隨本秩，祭以牲牢。

translations.literal: After the harvest, each according to its original rank was sacrificed to with the full pen.
translations.idiomatic: After the harvest, each according to its original rank was sacrificed to with the full pen.

sentences.zh: 至是，羣祀先廢者皆復之。

translations.literal: By then, all collective cults previously abolished were restored.
translations.idiomatic: By then all collective cults previously abolished were restored.

sentences.zh: 顯祖皇興二年，以青徐既平，遣中書令兼太常高允奉玉幣祀於東岳，以太牢祀孔子。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangxing under Emperor Xianzu, as Qing and Xu had been pacified, Director of the Secretariat and concurrent Director of Ritual Gao Yun was sent with jade and silk to sacrifice at the Eastern Peak, and to sacrifice to Confucius with the great pen.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huangxing under Emperor Xianzu, as Qing and Xu had been pacified, Director of the Secretariat and concurrent Director of Ritual Gao Yun was sent with jade and silk to sacrifice at the Eastern Peak and to sacrifice to Confucius with the great pen.

sentences.zh: 高祖延興二年，有司奏天地五郊、社稷已下及諸神，合一千七十五所，歲用牲七萬五千五百。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanxing under Emperor Gaozu, the responsible officials reported that Heaven and Earth, the Five Suburban Altars, the Altar of Soil and Grain, and all spirits below totaled 1,075 sites, using 75,500 victims per year.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yanxing under Emperor Gaozu, the responsible officials reported that Heaven and Earth, the Five Suburban Altars, the Altar of Soil and Grain, and all spirits below totaled 1,075 sites, consuming 75,500 victims each year.

sentences.zh: 顯祖深愍生命，乃詔曰：「朕承天事神，以育羣品，而咸秩處廣，用牲甚眾。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu deeply pitied living creatures and therefore issued an edict: "We undertake Heaven's affairs and serve the spirits to nurture the multitude; yet because everywhere rites are performed, victims are extremely numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu deeply pitied living creatures and therefore issued an edict: "We undertake Heaven's affairs and serve the spirits to nurture the multitude; yet because rites are performed everywhere, victims are extremely numerous.

sentences.zh: 夫神聰明正直，享德與信，何必在牲。

translations.literal: Spirits are bright, upright, and discerning—they partake of virtue and faith. Why must it depend on victims.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits are bright, upright, and discerning—they partake of virtue and faith. Why must sacrifice depend on victims.

sentences.zh: 易曰：『東隣殺牛，不如西隣之礿祭，實受其福。』

translations.literal: The Changes says: 'The eastern neighbor slaughters an ox—it is not as good as the western neighbor's spring sacrifice; he truly receives its blessing.'
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says: 'The eastern neighbor slaughters an ox—it is not as good as the western neighbor's spring sacrifice; he truly receives its blessing.'

sentences.zh: 苟誠感有著，雖行潦菜羹，可以致大嘏，何必多殺，然後獲祉福哉！

translations.literal: If sincerity and feeling are truly manifest, even water gathered in roadside ruts and vegetable broth can bring great blessings—why must one slaughter many before obtaining good fortune!
translations.idiomatic: If sincerity and feeling are truly manifest, even water gathered in roadside ruts and vegetable broth can bring great blessings—why must one slaughter many victims before obtaining good fortune!

sentences.zh: 其命有司，非郊天地、宗廟、社稷之祀，皆無用牲。」

translations.literal: Order the responsible officials: for all sacrifices except those to Heaven and Earth at the suburbs, the ancestral temples, and the Altar of Soil and Grain—none shall use victims."
translations.idiomatic: Order the responsible officials that for all sacrifices except those to Heaven and Earth at the suburbs, the ancestral temples, and the Altar of Soil and Grain, no victims shall be used."

sentences.zh: 於是羣祀悉用酒脯。

translations.literal: Thereupon all collective cults used only wine and dried meat.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon all collective cults used only wine and dried meat.

sentences.zh: 先是，長安牧守常有事於周文、武廟。

translations.literal: Before this, the governors and defenders of Chang'an regularly performed rites at the temples of Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, the governors and defenders of Chang'an regularly performed rites at the temples of Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，坎地埋牲，廟玉發見。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when sacrificial pits were dug and victims buried, temple jade appeared.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when pits were dug to bury victims, temple jade was revealed.

sentences.zh: 四月，詔東陽王丕祭文、武二廟。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Prince Dongyang Pi was ordered to sacrifice at the two temples of Wen and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, Prince Dongyang Pi was ordered to sacrifice at the two temples of Wen and Wu.

sentences.zh: 以廟玉露見，若即而埋之，或恐愚民將為盜竊，敕近司收之府藏。

translations.literal: Because the temple jade had been exposed and would be buried again, there was fear ignorant people might steal it; he ordered nearby officials to collect it for the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Because the temple jade had been exposed and would otherwise be buried again, there was fear that ignorant people might steal it, so he ordered nearby officials to collect it for the treasury.

sentences.zh: 六月，顯祖以西郊舊事，歲增木主七，易世則更兆，其事無益於神明。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Emperor Xianzu, regarding the old custom at the Western Suburb of adding seven wooden tablets each year and changing the site with every change of reign, judged the practice useless to the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Emperor Xianzu, regarding the old Western Suburb custom of adding seven wooden tablets each year and changing the site with every change of reign, judged the practice useless to the spirits.

sentences.zh: 初革前儀，定置主七，立碑於郊所。

translations.literal: He first reformed the former rite, fixing seven tablets in place, and erected a stele at the suburban site.
translations.idiomatic: He first reformed the former rite, fixing seven tablets in place, and erected a stele at the suburban site.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，旱。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe, drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taihe there was drought.

sentences.zh: 帝親祈皇天、日月五星於苑中，祭之夕大雨，遂赦京師。

translations.literal: The emperor personally prayed to August Heaven, the sun, moon, and Five Planets in the park; on the evening of sacrifice great rain fell, and he thereupon pardoned the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally prayed to August Heaven, the sun, moon, and Five Planets in the park; on the evening of the sacrifice great rain fell, and he thereupon pardoned the capital.

sentences.zh: 三年，上祈於北苑，又禱星於苑中。

translations.literal: In the third year the emperor prayed at the Northern Park, and again prayed to the stars in the park.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the emperor prayed at the Northern Park and again prayed to the stars in the park.

sentences.zh: 六年十一月，將親祀七廟，詔有司依禮具儀。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the sixth year, as he was about to personally sacrifice at the Seven Temples, he ordered officials according to ritual to prepare the full rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the sixth year, as he was about to personally sacrifice at the Seven Temples, he ordered officials to prepare the full rites according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 於是羣官議曰：「昔有虞親虔，祖考來格；

translations.literal: Thereupon the assembled officials deliberated, saying: "In antiquity You personally and reverently—ancestors and fathers came;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the assembled officials deliberated, saying: "In antiquity You personally and reverently attended sacrifice, and ancestors and fathers came;

sentences.zh: 殷宗躬謁，介福逌降。

translations.literal: Yin Zong personally attended—great blessings descended promptly.
translations.idiomatic: the Yin sovereign personally attended, and great blessings descended promptly.

sentences.zh: 大魏七廟之祭，依先朝舊事，多不親謁。

translations.literal: Sacrifice at the Seven Temples of Great Wei, following former dynastic practice, mostly did not involve personal attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice at the Seven Temples of Great Wei, following former dynastic practice, mostly did not involve the emperor's personal attendance.

sentences.zh: 今陛下孝誠發中，思親祀事，稽合古王禮之常典。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty's filial sincerity rises from within; you think of personally attending sacrifice—a thing that accords with the constant canon of ancient royal ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty's filial sincerity rises from within; you think of personally attending sacrifice—a thing that accords with the constant canon of ancient royal ritual.

sentences.zh: 臣等謹案舊章，并採漢魏故事，撰祭服冠屨牲牢之具，罍洗簠簋俎豆之器，百官助祭位次，樂官節奏之引，升降進退之法，別集為親拜之儀。」

translations.literal: We your servants respectfully examine former regulations and also gather precedents from Han and Wei, composing details of sacrificial robes, caps, shoes, and full-pen victims, vessels of washbasin, pure water, grain baskets, meat stands, and offering cups, seating order for all officials assisting sacrifice, cues of rhythm for music officers, and methods of ascending, descending, advancing, and withdrawing—compiling these separately into rites for personal obeisance."
translations.idiomatic: We your servants respectfully examine former regulations and also gather precedents from Han and Wei, composing the details of sacrificial robes, caps, shoes, and full-pen victims, the vessels of washbasin, pure water, grain baskets, meat stands, and offering cups, the seating order for all officials assisting sacrifice, the rhythmic cues for music officers, and the methods of ascending, descending, advancing, and withdrawing—compiling these separately into rites for personal obeisance."

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 於是上乃親祭。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor personally performed sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the emperor personally performed sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 其後四時常祀，皆親之。

translations.literal: Thereafter at the regular seasonal sacrifices he always attended in person.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter at the regular seasonal sacrifices he always attended in person.

sentences.zh: 十年四月，帝初以法服御輦，祀於西郊。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the tenth year, the emperor for the first time wore formal robes and rode in the imperial carriage to sacrifice at the Western Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the tenth year, the emperor for the first time wore formal robes and rode in the imperial carriage to sacrifice at the Western Suburb.

sentences.zh: 十二年閏九月，帝親築圓丘於南郊。

translations.literal: In the intercalary ninth month of the twelfth year, the emperor personally built a round mound at the Southern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary ninth month of the twelfth year, the emperor personally built a round mound at the Southern Suburb.

translations.literal: The text is deficient.
translations.idiomatic: The text is deficient.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月，帝以大駕有事於圓丘。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year, the emperor with the full imperial procession performed rites at the round mound.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirteenth year, the emperor with the full imperial procession performed rites at the round mound.

sentences.zh: 五月庚戌，車駕有事於方澤。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the fifth month, the imperial carriage performed rites at the square pond.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu in the fifth month, the imperial carriage performed rites at the square pond.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，高祖臨皇信堂，引見羣臣。

translations.literal: On renxu, Emperor Gaozu came to the Hall of Imperial Trust and received the officials in audience.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Emperor Gaozu came to the Hall of Imperial Trust and received the officials in audience.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「禮記祭法稱：『有虞氏禘黃帝。』

translations.literal: He issued an edict: "The Record of Rites, Sacrificial Canon, says: 'You performed the di sacrifice to the Yellow Emperor.'
translations.idiomatic: He issued an edict: "The Record of Rites, Sacrificial Canon, says: 'You performed the di sacrifice to the Yellow Emperor.'

sentences.zh: 大傳曰『禘其祖之所自出』，又稱『不王不禘』。

translations.literal: The Great Tradition says, 'Perform di to the ancestor from whom one's line descends,' and again says, 'Without being king, one does not perform di.'
translations.idiomatic: The Great Tradition says, 'Perform di to the ancestor from whom one's line descends,' and again says, 'Without being king, one does not perform di.'

sentences.zh: 論曰：『禘自既灌。』

translations.literal: The Analects says: 'Di begins after the libation has been poured.'
translations.idiomatic: The Analects says: 'Di begins after the libation has been poured.'

sentences.zh: 詩頌：『長發，大禘。』

translations.literal: The Odes, Hymns: 'Changfa—great di.'
translations.idiomatic: The Odes, Hymns: 'Changfa—great di.'

sentences.zh: 爾雅曰：『禘，大祭也。』

translations.literal: The Erya says: 'Di is a great sacrifice.'
translations.idiomatic: The Erya says: 'Di is a great sacrifice.'

sentences.zh: 夏殷四時祭：礿、禘、烝、嘗，周改禘為礿。

translations.literal: The Xia and Yin seasonal sacrifices were yue, di, zheng, and chang; Zhou changed di to yue.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia and Yin seasonal sacrifices were yue, di, zheng, and chang; Zhou changed di to yue.

sentences.zh: 祭義稱『春禘、秋嘗』，亦夏殷祭也。

translations.literal: [12] The Meaning of Sacrifice says 'spring di, autumn chang,' [13] which are also the Xia and Yin sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: [12] The Meaning of Sacrifice says 'spring di, autumn chang,' [13] which are also the Xia and Yin sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 王制稱：『犆礿、祫禘、祫嘗、祫烝。』

translations.literal: The Royal Regulations say: 'sole yue, xia di, xia chang, and xia zheng.'
translations.idiomatic: The Royal Regulations say: 'sole yue, xia di, xia chang, and xia zheng.'

sentences.zh: 其禮傳之文如此。

translations.literal: Such are the words of the ritual texts.
translations.idiomatic: Such are the words of the ritual texts.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄解禘，天子祭圓丘曰禘，祭宗廟大祭亦曰禘。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan explained di thus: when the Son of Heaven sacrifices at the Round Mound it is called di, and when he performs the great sacrifice in the ancestral temple it is also called di.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan explained di thus: when the Son of Heaven sacrifices at the Round Mound it is called di, and when he performs the great sacrifice in the ancestral temple it is also called di.

sentences.zh: 三年一祫，五年一禘。

translations.literal: Xia is performed once every three years, di once every five years.
translations.idiomatic: Xia is performed once every three years, di once every five years.

sentences.zh: 祫則合羣毀廟之主於太廟，合而祭之。

translations.literal: In xia, the spirit tablets of all shrines whose temples have been abolished are assembled in the Grand Temple and sacrificed to together.
translations.idiomatic: In xia, the spirit tablets of all abolished shrines are gathered in the Grand Temple and sacrificed to as one.

sentences.zh: 禘則增及百官配食者，審諦而祭之。

translations.literal: In di, officials whose tablets share the sacrifice are included as well, and sacrifice is performed with careful scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: In di, the tablets of officials who share the sacrifice are also included, and the rite is performed with meticulous scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 天子先禘祫而後時祭，諸侯先時祭而後禘祫。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven performs di and xia before the seasonal sacrifices; feudal lords perform seasonal sacrifices before di and xia.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven performs di and xia before the seasonal sacrifices; feudal lords perform the seasonal sacrifices before di and xia.

sentences.zh: 魯禮，三年喪畢而祫，明年而禘。

translations.literal: In Lu's ritual, xia came when the three-year mourning was completed, and di the year after.
translations.idiomatic: In Lu's ritual, xia was performed when the three-year mourning ended, and di the following year.

sentences.zh: 圓丘、宗廟大祭俱稱禘，祭有兩禘明也。

translations.literal: Both the Round Mound and the great ancestral temple sacrifice are called di—clearly there are two kinds of di sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Both the Round Mound and the great ancestral temple sacrifice are called di—clearly there are two distinct di sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 王肅解禘祫，稱天子諸侯皆禘於宗廟，非祭天之祭。

translations.literal: Wang Su explained di and xia, saying that the Son of Heaven and feudal lords all perform di in the ancestral temple—it is not a sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su explained di and xia, holding that the Son of Heaven and feudal lords all perform di in the ancestral temple—it is not a sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 郊祀后稷，不稱禘，宗廟稱禘。

translations.literal: Sacrifice to Hou Ji at the suburban rites is not called di; in the ancestral temple it is called di.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to Hou Ji at the suburban rites is not called di; in the ancestral temple it is called di.

sentences.zh: 禘、祫一名也，合而祭之故稱祫，審諦之故稱禘，非兩祭之名。

translations.literal: Di and xia are one name: because the shrines are combined for sacrifice it is called xia; because the rite is scrutinized carefully it is called di—they are not the names of two separate sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Di and xia are one name: because the shrines are combined for sacrifice it is called xia; because the rite is scrutinized with care it is called di—they are not the names of two separate sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 三年一祫，五年一禘，總而互舉之，故稱五年再殷祭，不言一禘一祫，斷可知矣。

translations.literal: Xia once every three years and di once every five years are taken altogether and alternately mentioned, hence it is called 'two grand sacrifices in five years,' without speaking of one di and one xia separately—from this one can know with certainty.
translations.idiomatic: Xia every three years and di every five years are counted together and mentioned in turn, hence the phrase 'two grand sacrifices in five years'—without speaking of one di and one xia separately. From this the point is clear.

sentences.zh: 禮文大略，諸儒之說，盡具於此。

translations.literal: The gist of the ritual texts and the explanations of the scholars are all presented here.
translations.idiomatic: The gist of the ritual texts and the scholars' explanations are all set forth here.

sentences.zh: 卿等便可議其是非。」

translations.literal: You ministers may now debate their right and wrong."
translations.idiomatic: You ministers may now debate which view is correct."

sentences.zh: 尚書游明根、左丞郭祚、中書侍郎封琳、著作郎崔光等對曰：「鄭氏之義，禘者大祭之名。

translations.literal: Minister You Minggen, Left Assistant Director Guo Zuo, Secretariat Vice Director Feng Lin, Director of Compilation Cui Guang, and others replied: "In Master Zheng's interpretation, di is the name of a great sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Minister You Minggen, Left Assistant Director Guo Zuo, Secretariat Vice Director Feng Lin, Director of Compilation Cui Guang, and others replied: "In Master Zheng's interpretation, di is the name of a great sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 大祭圓丘謂之禘者，審諦五精星辰也；

translations.literal: The great sacrifice at the Round Mound is called di because the Five Essences and stars are scrutinized carefully;
translations.idiomatic: The great sacrifice at the Round Mound is called di because the Five Essences and the stars are scrutinized with care;

sentences.zh: 大祭宗廟謂之禘者，審諦其昭穆。

translations.literal: the great sacrifice in the ancestral temple is called di because senior and junior lineage order is scrutinized carefully.
translations.idiomatic: the great sacrifice in the ancestral temple is called di because senior and junior lineage order is scrutinized with care.

sentences.zh: 圓丘常合不言祫，宗廟時合故言祫。

translations.literal: At the Round Mound the rites are always combined, so xia is not mentioned; in the ancestral temple they are combined only at certain times, hence xia is mentioned.
translations.idiomatic: At the Round Mound the rites are always combined, so xia is not mentioned; in the ancestral temple they are combined only at certain times, hence xia is mentioned.

sentences.zh: 斯則宗廟祫禘並行，圓丘一禘而已。

translations.literal: Thus in the ancestral temple xia and di are performed together, while at the Round Mound there is only one di.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in the ancestral temple xia and di are performed together, while at the Round Mound there is only one di.

sentences.zh: 宜於宗廟俱行禘祫之禮。

translations.literal: Both di and xia rites ought to be performed together in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Both di and xia rites ought to be performed together in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 二禮異，故名殊。

translations.literal: The two rites differ, and so their names differ.
translations.idiomatic: The two rites differ, and so their names differ.

sentences.zh: 依禮，春廢犆礿，於嘗於蒸則祫，不於三時皆行禘祫之禮。」

translations.literal: According to ritual, in spring the sole yue is omitted; at chang and zheng xia is performed—not at all three seasons are di and xia rites carried out."
translations.idiomatic: According to ritual, in spring the sole yue is omitted; at chang and zheng xia is performed—the di and xia rites are not carried out in all three seasons."

sentences.zh: [14]中書監高閭、儀曹令李韶、中書侍郎高遵等十三人對稱：「禘祭圓丘之禘與鄭義同，其宗廟禘祫之祭與王義同。

translations.literal: [14] Secretariat Director Gao Lu, Director of Rituals Li Shao, Secretariat Vice Director Gao Zun, and thirteen others replied: "The di sacrifice at the Round Mound accords with Master Zheng's interpretation; the di and xia sacrifices in the ancestral temple accord with Master Wang's interpretation.
translations.idiomatic: [14] Secretariat Director Gao Lu, Director of Rituals Li Shao, Secretariat Vice Director Gao Zun, and thirteen others replied: "The di sacrifice at the Round Mound accords with Master Zheng's interpretation; the di and xia sacrifices in the ancestral temple accord with Master Wang's interpretation.

sentences.zh: 與鄭義同者，以為有虞禘黃帝，黃帝非虞在廟之帝，不在廟，非圓丘而何？

translations.literal: What accords with Master Zheng is this: Yu performed di to the Yellow Emperor; the Yellow Emperor was not an emperor of Yu enshrined in the temple—if not in the temple, what could it be but the Round Mound?
translations.idiomatic: What accords with Master Zheng is this: Yu performed di to the Yellow Emperor; the Yellow Emperor was not an emperor of Yu enshrined in the temple—if not in the temple, what could it be but the Round Mound?

sentences.zh: 又大傳稱祖其所自出之祖，又非在廟之文。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Great Tradition speaks of di to the ancestor from whom one's line descends—again, not language about one enshrined in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Great Tradition speaks of di to the ancestor from whom one's line descends—again, not language about one enshrined in the temple.

sentences.zh: 論稱『禘自既灌』，事似據。
