translations.literal: The Analects says 'Di begins after the libation has been poured'—the matter seems to have textual support.
translations.idiomatic: The Analects says 'Di begins after the libation has been poured'—the matter seems to have textual support.

sentences.zh: 爾雅稱『禘，大祭也』。

translations.literal: The Erya says 'Di is a great sacrifice.'
translations.idiomatic: The Erya says 'Di is a great sacrifice.'

sentences.zh: 頌『長發，大禘也』，殷王之祭。

translations.literal: The hymn 'Changfa—great di' is the sacrifice of the Yin kings.
translations.idiomatic: The hymn 'Changfa—great di' describes the sacrifice of the Yin kings.

sentences.zh: 斯皆非諸侯之禮，諸侯無禘。

translations.literal: These are none of them the rites of feudal lords—feudal lords have no di.
translations.idiomatic: None of these are the rites of feudal lords—feudal lords do not perform di.

sentences.zh: 禮唯夏殷，夏祭稱禘，又非宗廟之禘。

translations.literal: Ritual speaks only of Xia and Yin; the Xia sacrifice was called di, and again this was not the di of the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual speaks only of Xia and Yin; the Xia sacrifice was called di, and again this was not the di of the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 魯行天子之儀，不敢專行圓丘之禘，改殷之禘，取其禘名於宗廟，因先有祫，遂生兩名。

translations.literal: Lu followed the Son of Heaven's rites but dared not perform the Round Mound di on its own; it changed Yin's di, borrowing the name di for the ancestral temple, and because xia already existed, two names arose.
translations.idiomatic: Lu followed the Son of Heaven's rites but dared not perform the Round Mound di on its own; it changed Yin's di, borrowing the name di for the ancestral temple, and because xia already existed, two names arose.

sentences.zh: 據王氏之義，祫而禘祭之，故言禘祫，總謂再殷祭，明不異也。

translations.literal: According to Master Wang's interpretation, xia is performed as di sacrifice, hence the term di-xia; taken together this means two grand sacrifices, showing they are not different.
translations.idiomatic: According to Master Wang's interpretation, xia is performed as di sacrifice, hence the term di-xia; taken together this means two grand sacrifices, showing they are not different.

sentences.zh: 禘祫一名也。

translations.literal: Di and xia are one name.
translations.idiomatic: Di and xia are one name.

sentences.zh: 其禘祫止於一時，止於一時者，祭不欲數，數則黷。

translations.literal: Di and xia are limited to one season; they are limited to one season because sacrifice should not be frequent—if frequent, it becomes irreverent.
translations.idiomatic: Di and xia are limited to one season, because sacrifice should not be frequent—if performed too often, it becomes irreverent.

sentences.zh: 一歲而三禘，愚以為過數。」

translations.literal: Three di sacrifices in one year—we consider this excessive in frequency."
translations.idiomatic: Three di sacrifices in one year—we consider that excessive."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「尚書、中書等，據二家之義，論禘祫詳矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Ministers and secretariat officials, relying on the interpretations of both schools, have debated di and xia in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Ministers and secretariat officials, relying on the interpretations of both schools, have debated di and xia in detail.

sentences.zh: 然於行事取衷，猶有未允。

translations.literal: Yet in choosing a middle course for practice, there are still points that do not satisfy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in choosing a practical middle course, there are still points that do not satisfy.

sentences.zh: 監等以禘祫為名，義同王氏，禘祭圓丘，事與鄭同。

translations.literal: The director and others take di and xia as one name, in meaning agreeing with Master Wang; di sacrifice at the Round Mound, in practice agreeing with Master Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: The director and others take di and xia as one name, in meaning agreeing with Master Wang; di sacrifice at the Round Mound, in practice agreeing with Master Zheng.

sentences.zh: 無所間然。

translations.literal: On these there is nothing to question.
translations.idiomatic: On these there is nothing to question.

sentences.zh: 尚書等與鄭氏同，兩名兩祭，並存並用，理有未稱。

translations.literal: The ministers and others agree with Master Zheng—two names, two sacrifices, both preserved and both used—the reasoning is not fully adequate.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers and others agree with Master Zheng—two names, two sacrifices, both preserved and both used—the reasoning is not fully adequate.

sentences.zh: 俱據二義，一時禘祫，而闕二時之禘，事有難從。

translations.literal: Both rely on the two interpretations, performing di and xia in one season while omitting di in the other two seasons—this is hard to follow in practice.
translations.idiomatic: Both rely on the two interpretations, performing di and xia in one season while omitting di in the other two seasons—this is hard to follow in practice.

sentences.zh: 夫先王制禮，內緣人子之情，外恊尊卑之序。

translations.literal: When the former kings fashioned ritual, inwardly they followed the feelings of a son, outwardly they harmonized the order of senior and junior.
translations.idiomatic: When the former kings fashioned ritual, inwardly they followed a son's feelings, outwardly they harmonized the order of senior and junior.

sentences.zh: 故天子七廟，諸侯五廟，大夫三廟，數盡則毀，藏主於太祖之廟，三年而祫祭之。

translations.literal: Hence the Son of Heaven had seven shrines, feudal lords five, grand officers three; when the number was full a shrine was abolished, its tablet stored in the shrine of the Great Ancestor, and xia sacrifice performed every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Son of Heaven had seven shrines, feudal lords five, and grand officers three; when the number was full a shrine was abolished, its tablet stored in the shrine of the Great Ancestor, and xia sacrifice was performed every three years.

sentences.zh: 世盡則毀，以示有終之義；

translations.literal: When generations were exhausted a shrine was abolished, to show the principle that all things have an end;
translations.idiomatic: When generations were exhausted a shrine was abolished, to show that all things have an end;

sentences.zh: 三年而祫，以申追遠之情。

translations.literal: xia every three years, to express the feeling of honoring the distant past.
translations.idiomatic: xia every three years, to express the feeling of honoring the distant past.

sentences.zh: 禘祫既是一祭，分而兩之，事無所據。

translations.literal: Since di and xia are one sacrifice, to divide them into two has no basis in practice.
translations.idiomatic: Since di and xia are one sacrifice, dividing them into two has no basis in practice.

sentences.zh: 毀廟三年一祫，又有不盡四時，於禮為闕。

translations.literal: Abolished shrines receive xia once every three years, and moreover not all four seasons are covered—in ritual this is deficient.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished shrines receive xia once every three years, and moreover not all four seasons are covered—in ritual terms this is deficient.

sentences.zh: 七廟四時常祭，祫則三年一祭，而又不究四時，於情為簡。

translations.literal: The seven shrines have regular seasonal sacrifices in all four seasons, while xia is once every three years and again does not cover all four seasons—in feeling this is too spare.
translations.idiomatic: The seven shrines have regular seasonal sacrifices in all four seasons, while xia is once every three years and again does not cover all four seasons—in human feeling this is too spare.

sentences.zh: 王以禘祫為一祭，王義為長。

translations.literal: Master Wang takes di and xia as one sacrifice—Master Wang's interpretation is superior.
translations.idiomatic: Master Wang takes di and xia as one sacrifice—Master Wang's interpretation is superior.

sentences.zh: 鄭以圓丘為禘，與宗廟大祭同名，義亦為當。

translations.literal: Master Zheng takes the Round Mound as di, sharing the name with the great ancestral temple sacrifice—this interpretation is also fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Master Zheng takes the Round Mound as di, sharing the name with the great ancestral temple sacrifice—this interpretation is also fitting.

sentences.zh: 今互取鄭、王二義。

translations.literal: Now we shall take from both Master Zheng's and Master Wang's interpretations.
translations.idiomatic: Now we shall take from both Master Zheng's and Master Wang's interpretations.

sentences.zh: 禘祫并為一名，從王；

translations.literal: Di and xia together as one name—following Master Wang;
translations.idiomatic: Di and xia together as one name—following Master Wang;

sentences.zh: 禘是祭圓丘大祭之名，上下同用，從鄭。

translations.literal: di is the name of the great sacrifice at the Round Mound, used alike above and below—following Master Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: di is the name of the great sacrifice at the Round Mound, used alike above and below—following Master Zheng.

sentences.zh: 若以數則黷，五年一禘，改祫從禘。

translations.literal: If frequency makes sacrifice irreverent, then di once every five years—change xia to follow di.
translations.idiomatic: If frequency makes sacrifice irreverent, then di once every five years—change xia to follow di.

sentences.zh: 五年一禘，則四時盡禘，以稱今情。

translations.literal: Di once every five years will cover all four seasons with di, suiting present sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Di once every five years will cover all four seasons with di, suiting present sentiment.

sentences.zh: 禘則依禮文，先禘而後時祭。

translations.literal: For di, follow the ritual texts: perform di before the seasonal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: For di, follow the ritual texts: perform di before the seasonal sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 便即施行，著之於令，永為世法。」

translations.literal: Implement this at once, record it in edict, and make it the law for all generations."
translations.idiomatic: Implement this at once, record it in edict, and make it the law for all generations."

sentences.zh: 高閭曰：[16]「書稱：『肆類于上帝，禋于六宗。』

translations.literal: Gao Lu said: [16] "The Documents say: 'Perform the si rite to August Heaven, and the yin rite to the Six Honored Ones.'
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu said: [16] "The Documents say: 'Perform the si rite to August Heaven, and the yin rite to the Six Honored Ones.'

sentences.zh: 六宗之祀，禮無明文，名位壇兆，歷代所疑。

translations.literal: Sacrifice to the Six Honored Ones has no explicit text in ritual; their names, ranks, altars, and sites have been doubted by every generation.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to the Six Honored Ones has no explicit text in ritual; their names, ranks, altars, and sites have been doubted by every generation.

sentences.zh: 漢魏及晉諸儒異說，或稱天地四時，或稱六者之間，或稱易之六子，或稱風雷之類，或稱星辰之屬，或曰世代所宗，或云宗廟所尚，或曰社稷五祀，凡有十一家。

translations.literal: Han, Wei, and Jin scholars offered differing views: some called them Heaven, Earth, and the four seasons; some the spaces between the six; some the six sons of the Changes; some wind, thunder, and the like; some stars and constellations; some said what each age revered; some said what the ancestral temple honored; some said the five sacrifices of the altars of soil and grain—in all eleven schools.
translations.idiomatic: Han, Wei, and Jin scholars offered differing views: some called them Heaven, Earth, and the four seasons; some the spaces between the six; some the six sons of the Changes; some wind, thunder, and the like; some stars and constellations; some said what each age revered; some said what the ancestral temple honored; some said the five sacrifices of the altars of soil and grain—in all eleven schools.

sentences.zh: 自晉已來，逮于聖世，以為論者雖多，皆有所闕，莫能評究。

translations.literal: From Jin down to the present sage age, though commentators were many, all had gaps and none could fully evaluate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: From Jin down to the present sage age, though commentators were many, all had gaps and none could fully evaluate the matter.

sentences.zh: 遂相因承，別立六宗之兆，總為一位而祭之。

translations.literal: They therefore followed one another, separately establishing sites for the Six Honored Ones and sacrificing to them as one combined seat.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore followed one another, separately establishing sites for the Six Honored Ones and sacrificing to them as one combined seat.

sentences.zh: 比敕臣等評議取衷，附之祀典。

translations.literal: Recently Your Majesty ordered us to debate and choose a middle course, and append it to the sacrificial canon.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Your Majesty ordered us to debate and choose a middle course, and append it to the sacrificial canon.

sentences.zh: 臣等承旨，披究往說，各有其理。

translations.literal: We your servants received the edict, examined past explanations, and found each had its reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: We your servants received the edict, examined past explanations, and found each had its reasoning.

sentences.zh: 較而論之，長短互有，若偏用一家，事或差舛。

translations.literal: Comparing them, each has strengths and weaknesses; if one school alone were adopted, practice might go astray.
translations.idiomatic: Comparing them, each has strengths and weaknesses; if one school alone were adopted, practice might go astray.

sentences.zh: 眾疑則從多，今惑則仍古。

translations.literal: When many doubt, follow the majority; when doubt remains today, keep the ancient practice.
translations.idiomatic: When many doubt, follow the majority; when doubt remains today, keep the ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 請依先別處六宗之兆，總為一祀而祭之。」

translations.literal: We ask to follow the former practice of separately establishing sites for the Six Honored Ones and sacrificing to them as one combined rite."
translations.idiomatic: We ask to follow the former practice of separately establishing sites for the Six Honored Ones and sacrificing to them as one combined rite."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「詳定朝令，祀為事首，以疑從疑，何所取正？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When drafting court edicts in detail, sacrifice is the foremost affair—if doubt follows doubt, what standard can be taken as correct?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "When drafting court edicts in detail, sacrifice is the foremost affair—if doubt follows doubt, what standard can be taken as correct?

sentences.zh: 昔石渠、虎閤之議，皆準類以引義，原事以證情，故能通百家之要，定累世之疑。

translations.literal: In former days the debates at Shiqu and Huke all matched categories to draw out principle and traced matters to verify sentiment, and so could penetrate the essentials of the hundred schools and settle doubts accumulated over generations.
translations.idiomatic: In former days the debates at Shiqu and Huke all matched categories to draw out principle and traced matters to verify sentiment, and so could penetrate the essentials of the hundred schools and settle doubts accumulated over generations.

sentences.zh: 況今有文可據，有本可推，而不評而定之，其致安在？

translations.literal: Moreover, today there are texts to rely on and origins to trace—if one does not evaluate and decide, where is the point in this?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, today there are texts to rely on and origins to trace—if one does not evaluate and decide, where is the point in this?

sentences.zh: 朕躬覽尚書之文，稱『肆類上帝，禋於六宗』，文相連屬，理似一事。

translations.literal: I have personally read the text of the Documents, which says 'Perform the si rite to August Heaven, and the yin rite to the Six Honored Ones'—the words are linked together, and the reasoning seems to concern one affair.
translations.idiomatic: I have personally read the text of the Documents, which says 'Perform the si rite to August Heaven, and the yin rite to the Six Honored Ones'—the words are linked together, and the reasoning seems to concern one affair.

sentences.zh: 上帝稱肆而無禋，六宗言禋而不別其名。

translations.literal: August Heaven is called si but not yin; the Six Honored Ones are called yin but their names are not distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: August Heaven is called si but not yin; the Six Honored Ones are called yin but their names are not distinguished.

sentences.zh: 以此推之，上帝、六宗當是一時之祀，非別祭之名。

translations.literal: Inferring from this, August Heaven and the Six Honored Ones must be one sacrifice at one time—not the names of separate sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Inferring from this, August Heaven and the Six Honored Ones must be one sacrifice at one time—not the names of separate sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 肆類非獨祭之目，焚煙非他祀之用。

translations.literal: Si and lei are not terms for a sacrifice alone; burning incense smoke is not used for other sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Si and lei are not terms for a sacrifice alone; burning incense smoke is not used for other sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 六宗者，必是天皇大帝及五帝之神明矣。

translations.literal: The Six Honored Ones must be the Heavenly August Emperor and the spirits of the Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Honored Ones must be the Heavenly August Emperor and the spirits of the Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 禋是祭帝之事，故稱禋以關其他，故稱六以證之。

translations.literal: Yin is the act of sacrificing to emperors; hence yin is named to connect with the others, and six is named to verify this.
translations.idiomatic: Yin is the act of sacrificing to emperors; hence yin is named to connect with the others, and six is named to verify this.

sentences.zh: 然則肆類上帝，禋于六宗，一祭也，互舉以成之。

translations.literal: Thus 'Perform the si rite to August Heaven, and the yin rite to the Six Honored Ones' is one sacrifice, the terms mutually cited to complete it.
translations.idiomatic: Thus 'Perform the si rite to August Heaven, and the yin rite to the Six Honored Ones' is one sacrifice, the terms mutually cited to complete it.

sentences.zh: 今祭圓丘，五帝在焉，其牲幣俱禋，故稱肆類上帝，禋于六宗。

translations.literal: Today when sacrificing at the Round Mound, the Five Emperors are present there; victims and silks are all offered with yin, hence it is called 'Perform the si rite to August Heaven, and the yin rite to the Six Honored Ones.'
translations.idiomatic: Today when sacrificing at the Round Mound, the Five Emperors are present there; victims and silks are all offered with yin, hence it is called 'Perform the si rite to August Heaven, and the yin rite to the Six Honored Ones.'

sentences.zh: 一祭而六祀備焉。

translations.literal: One sacrifice, and all six sacrifices are complete.
translations.idiomatic: One sacrifice, and all six sacrifices are complete.

sentences.zh: 六祭既備，無煩復別立六宗之位。

translations.literal: Since the six sacrifices are complete, there is no need to establish separate seats for the Six Honored Ones.
translations.idiomatic: Since the six sacrifices are complete, there is no need to establish separate seats for the Six Honored Ones.

sentences.zh: 便可依此附令，永為定法。」

translations.literal: Let this be appended to edict accordingly and made the fixed law forever."
translations.idiomatic: Let this be appended to edict accordingly and made the fixed law forever."

sentences.zh: 十四年八月詔曰：「丘澤初志，[17]配尚宜定，五德相襲，分敍有常。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourteenth year an edict said: "The original intent of mound and pond sacrifice, [17] the pairing and honors ought to be fixed; the Five Virtues succeed one another, and their ordering has fixed norms.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourteenth year an edict said: "The original intent of mound and pond sacrifice, [17] the pairing and honors ought to be fixed; the Five Virtues succeed one another, and their ordering has fixed norms.

sentences.zh: 然異同之論，著於往漢，未詳之說，疑在今史。

translations.literal: Yet conflicting theories were recorded in former Han; unresolved explanations remain doubtful in present histories.
translations.idiomatic: Yet conflicting theories were recorded in former Han; unresolved explanations remain doubtful in present histories.

sentences.zh: 羣官百辟，可議其所應，必令合衷，以成萬代之式。」

translations.literal: All officials may debate what is appropriate, and it must accord with the middle course, to establish the model for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: All officials may debate what is appropriate, and it must accord with the middle course, to establish the model for ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 中書監高閭議以為：「帝王之作，百代可知，運代相承，書傳可驗。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Gao Lu argued: "The rise of emperors and kings can be known across a hundred generations; dynasties succeed one another, verifiable in written records.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Gao Lu argued: "The rise of emperors and kings can be known across a hundred generations; dynasties succeed one another, verifiable in written records.

sentences.zh: 雖祚命有長短，德政有優劣，至於受終嚴祖，殷薦上帝，其致一也。

translations.literal: Though fortunes may be long or short and governance good or poor, in receiving the end, honoring ancestors, and abundantly offering to August Heaven, the purpose is one.
translations.idiomatic: Though fortunes may be long or short and governance good or poor, in receiving the end, honoring ancestors, and abundantly offering to August Heaven, the purpose is one.

sentences.zh: 故敢述其前載，舉其大略。

translations.literal: Therefore I dare recount earlier records and set forth the general outline.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I dare recount earlier records and set forth the general outline.

sentences.zh: 臣聞居尊據極，允應明命者，莫不以中原為正統，神州為帝宅。

translations.literal: I have heard that those who occupy the highest place and truly respond to the bright mandate all take the Central Plains as orthodox succession and the divine land as the imperial domain.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that those who occupy the highest place and truly respond to the bright mandate all take the Central Plains as orthodox succession and the divine land as the imperial domain.

sentences.zh: 苟位當名全，化迹流洽，則不專以世數為與奪，善惡為是非。

translations.literal: If position matches name and transformation spreads widely, then one does not judge solely by number of generations for granting or withholding legitimacy, or by good and evil for right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: If position matches name and transformation spreads widely, then one does not judge solely by number of generations for granting or withholding legitimacy, or by good and evil for right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 故堯舜禪揖，一身異尚；

translations.literal: Hence Yao and Shun abdicated by yielding, yet in one person their honors differed;
translations.idiomatic: Hence Yao and Shun abdicated by yielding, yet in one person their honors differed;

sentences.zh: 魏晉相代，少紀運殊。

translations.literal: Wei and Jin succeeded one another, yet their brief reigns and fortunes differed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin succeeded one another, yet their brief reigns and fortunes differed.

sentences.zh: 桀紂至虐，不廢承歷之敍；

translations.literal: Jie and Zhou were utterly tyrannical, yet the sequence of succession was not abolished;
translations.idiomatic: Jie and Zhou were utterly tyrannical, yet the sequence of succession was not abolished;

sentences.zh: 厲惠至昏，不闕周晉之錄。

translations.literal: King Li and King Hui were utterly benighted, yet the records of Zhou and Jin were not omitted.
translations.idiomatic: King Li and King Hui were utterly benighted, yet the records of Zhou and Jin were not omitted.

sentences.zh: 計五德之論，始自漢劉，一時之議，三家致別。

translations.literal: Considering the theory of the Five Virtues, it began with Han Liu; in the debates of that age, three schools gave rise to divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Reckoning of the Five Virtues theory began with the Liu Han house; in the debates of that era, three rival schools gave differing accounts.

sentences.zh: 故張蒼以漢為水德，賈誼、公孫臣以漢為土德，劉向以漢為火德。

translations.literal: Thus Zhang Cang took Han as Water Virtue; Jia Yi and Gongsun Chen took Han as Earth Virtue; Liu Xiang took Han as Fire Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cang held that Han possessed Water Virtue; Jia Yi and Gongsun Chen held Earth Virtue; Liu Xiang held Fire Virtue.

sentences.zh: 以為水德者，正以嘗有水溢之應，則不推運代相承之數矣。

translations.literal: Those holding Water Virtue relied precisely on there having been a response of flooding waters, and did not reckon the numbers of dynasties succeeding in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: The Water Virtue school rested on omens of inundation and did not calculate the numerical sequence of dynastic succession.

sentences.zh: 以土德者，則以亡秦繼曆，相即為次，不推逆順之異也。

translations.literal: Those holding Earth Virtue took the extinguished Qin as succeeding the calendar, each immediately following as next in order, and did not reckon differences of reverse and direct succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Earth Virtue school treated fallen Qin as continuing the calendar in direct succession and did not weigh whether the transition ran forward or counter to the cycle.

sentences.zh: 以為火德者，懸證赤帝斬蛇之符，棄秦之暴，越惡承善，不以世次為正也，故以承周為火德。

translations.literal: Those holding Fire Virtue hung proof on the tally of the Red Emperor slaying the serpent, rejected Qin's cruelty, passed over evil to receive good, and did not take generational order as orthodox—hence taking succession from Zhou as Fire Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Fire Virtue advocates cited the legend of the Red Emperor and the slain serpent, repudiated Qin's tyranny, chose virtue over sequential inheritance, and therefore declared Han's succession from Zhou to be Fire Virtue.

sentences.zh: 自茲厥後，乃以為常。

translations.literal: From this time onward, it was taken as the constant practice.
translations.idiomatic: From that point forward, this became the established rule.

sentences.zh: 魏承漢，火生土，故魏為土德。

translations.literal: Wei succeeded Han; fire produces earth, hence Wei is Earth Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Wei succeeded Han—fire engenders earth—so Wei holds Earth Virtue.

sentences.zh: 晉承魏，土生金，故晉為金德。

translations.literal: Jin succeeded Wei; earth produces metal, hence Jin is Metal Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Jin succeeded Wei—earth engenders metal—so Jin holds Metal Virtue.

sentences.zh: 趙承晉，金生水，故趙為水德。

translations.literal: Zhao succeeded Jin; metal produces water, hence Zhao is Water Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao succeeded Jin—metal engenders water—so Zhao holds Water Virtue.

sentences.zh: 燕承趙，水生木，故燕為木德。

translations.literal: Yan succeeded Zhao; water produces wood, hence Yan is Wood Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yan succeeded Zhao—water engenders wood—so Yan holds Wood Virtue.

sentences.zh: 秦承燕，木生火，故秦為火德。

translations.literal: Qin succeeded Yan; wood produces fire, hence Qin is Fire Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Qin succeeded Yan—wood engenders fire—so Former Qin holds Fire Virtue.

sentences.zh: 秦之未滅，皇魏未克神州，秦氏既亡，大魏稱制玄朔。

translations.literal: Before Qin was extinguished, Imperial Wei had not yet conquered the divine land; once the Qin house fell, Great Wei assumed rule in the dark north.
translations.idiomatic: While Former Qin still stood, Imperial Wei had not yet won the Central Domain; once Qin perished, Great Wei established its mandate in the northern heartland.

sentences.zh: 故平文之廟，始稱『太祖』，以明受命之證，如周在岐之陽。

translations.literal: Therefore in Emperor Wen's temple they first styled him "Grand Ancestor," to clarify proof of receiving the mandate, as Zhou at Qi's south slope.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Emperor Wen's temple first took the title "Grand Ancestor," marking the receipt of Heaven's mandate—just as the Zhou rose south of Mount Qi.

sentences.zh: 若繼晉，晉亡已久；

translations.literal: If one were to succeed Jin, Jin has long been extinguished;
translations.idiomatic: To claim succession from Jin when Jin fell so long ago—

sentences.zh: 若棄秦，則中原有寄。

translations.literal: if one were to discard Qin, then the Central Plains would have a recipient.
translations.idiomatic: to discard Qin is to acknowledge where the Central Plains truly rested.

sentences.zh: 推此而言，承秦之理，事為明驗。

translations.literal: Pushing from this to speak, the principle of succeeding Qin is clearly verified in fact.
translations.idiomatic: Reasoning from this, the logic of succeeding Qin is plainly confirmed.

sentences.zh: 故以魏承秦，魏為土德，又五緯表驗，黃星曜彩，考氏定實，合德軒轅，承土祖未，事為著矣。

translations.literal: Therefore taking Wei as succeeding Qin, Wei is Earth Virtue; moreover the Five Planetary Conjunctions displayed verification, the Yellow Star shone with brilliance, clans were examined to fix reality, virtue matched the Yellow Emperor, inheriting Earth as ancestral virtue—the matter is clearly established.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Wei succeeds Qin as Earth Virtue—and the Five Conjunctions, the bright Yellow Star, examination of lineage, and correspondence with the Yellow Emperor's virtue all confirm it beyond dispute.

sentences.zh: 又秦趙及燕，雖非明聖，各正號赤縣，統有中土，郊天祭地，肆類咸秩，明刑制禮，不失舊章。

translations.literal: Moreover Qin, Zhao, and Yan, though not enlightened sages, each properly styled themselves in the red county, ruled the Central Lands, performed suburban sacrifice to Heaven and sacrifice to Earth, all categories of sacrifice in due order, clarified punishments and fashioned ritual, not losing the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Though Former Qin, Later Zhao, and the Yan states were no sage rulers, each claimed legitimate title over China, held the Central Lands, worshipped Heaven and Earth with full ceremonial order, and maintained law and ritual without abandoning received institutions.

sentences.zh: 奄岱踰河，境被淮漢。

translations.literal: Covering Mount Tai and crossing the Yellow River, their borders spread to the Huai and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Their domains stretched from Mount Tai across the Yellow River to the Huai and Han rivers.

sentences.zh: 非若齷齪邊方，僭擬之屬，遠如孫權、劉備，近若劉裕、道成，事繫蠻夷，非關中夏。

translations.literal: They were not like cramped border regions and usurping sorts—distant as Sun Quan and Liu Bei, or recent as Liu Yu and Xiao Daocheng—matters bound up with barbarians, not concerning the Central Xia.
translations.idiomatic: They were nothing like petty frontier regimes or pretenders—whether distant ones such as Sun Quan and Liu Bei or recent ones such as Liu Yu and Xiao Daocheng—whose affairs belong to the barbarian margins, not to the heartland of China.

sentences.zh: 伏惟聖朝，德配天地，道被四海，承乾統曆，功侔百王。

translations.literal: Bowing in reverence to the holy court: virtue matches Heaven and Earth, the Way spreads over the four seas, inheriting Qian and carrying the calendar, achievements equal the hundred kings.
translations.idiomatic: Your Sacred Majesty's virtue rivals Heaven and Earth, the Way pervades the four seas, the Mandate is upheld and the calendar maintained, and accomplishments match those of the sage kings of old.

sentences.zh: 光格同於唐虞，享祚流於周漢，正位中境，奄有萬方。

translations.literal: Bright transformation equals Tang and Yu, enjoyed fortune flows like Zhou and Han, occupying the orthodox center, covering the myriad regions.
translations.idiomatic: Its luminous governance equals that of Yao and Shun, its dynastic fortune endures like Zhou and Han, it holds the central throne and embraces all lands within the four seas.

sentences.zh: 今若并棄三家，遠承晉氏，則蔑中原正次之實。

translations.literal: Now if one altogether abandons the three houses and from afar succeeds the Jin clan, then one would scorn the reality of orthodox succession in the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: To discard all three dynasties and claim distant succession from Jin would slight the true order of legitimate succession in the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 存之無損於此，而有成於彼；

translations.literal: To preserve them would be no harm here, yet would accomplish there;
translations.idiomatic: Keeping them does this court no injury, yet brings completion elsewhere;

sentences.zh: 廢之無益於今，而有傷於事。

translations.literal: to abolish them would benefit not the present, yet would injure the affair.
translations.idiomatic: abolishing them profits nothing now, yet wounds what must be done.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜從尚黃，定為土德。

translations.literal: This humble minister thinks one ought to follow revering yellow and fix Earth Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant humbly holds that the court should honor yellow and establish Earth Virtue.

sentences.zh: 又前代之君，明賢之史，皆因其可褒褒之，可貶貶之。

translations.literal: Moreover, former ages' rulers and enlightened worthies among historians all praised where praise was due and censured where censure was due.
translations.idiomatic: Wise historians of past dynasties praised what deserved praise and condemned what deserved condemnation.

sentences.zh: 今議者偏據可絕之義，而不錄可全之禮。

translations.literal: Now the debaters one-sidedly rely on grounds for cutting off, yet do not record grounds for preserving ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Those debating today fixate on reasons to sever the line of succession and overlook the ritual grounds for preserving it.

sentences.zh: 所論事大，垂之萬葉。

translations.literal: What is debated is a great matter, to be handed down ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: This is a matter of the greatest consequence, to endure through ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 宜並集中秘羣儒，人人別議，擇其所長，於理為悉。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to gather together the palace scholars all at once, each debating separately, choosing their strengths—thus in principle the matter would be thorough."
translations.idiomatic: The court should assemble all the palace scholars for individual debate, take the best of each argument, and thereby reach the fullest understanding of principle."

sentences.zh: 秘書丞臣李彪、著作郎崔光等議以為：「尚書閭議，繼近秦氏。

translations.literal: Secretariat Assistant Minister Li Biao, Composition Director Cui Guang, and others argued: "Secretariat Director Lu's proposal succeeds the nearby Qin house.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Assistant Li Biao, Composition Director Cui Guang, and others submitted: "Director Lu's proposal would place our succession immediately after Former Qin.

sentences.zh: 臣職掌國籍，頗覽前書，惜此正次，慨彼非緒。

translations.literal: Your ministers' office manages the national archives; we have read former books extensively, regret this orthodox order, and grieve that improper lineage.
translations.idiomatic: We who keep the state archives have read widely in earlier histories; we lament what would be lost in the proper succession and mourn the false lineage it would embrace.

sentences.zh: 輒仰推帝始，遠尋百王。

translations.literal: We hastily look up to trace the imperial beginnings and seek far among the hundred kings.
translations.idiomatic: We have looked back to the founding of kingship and traced the lineage of rulers through antiquity.

sentences.zh: 魏雖建國君民，兆眹振古，祖黃制朔，緜迹有因。

translations.literal: Though Wei established the state and governed the people, its omens shook antiquity, it traced the Yellow Emperor to fashion the calendar, and its continuous traces have cause.
translations.idiomatic: Though Wei founded a realm and ruled the people, its portents reach back to antiquity; taking the Yellow Emperor as forebear and fixing the calendar, its succession follows clear precedent.

sentences.zh: 然此帝業，神元為首。

translations.literal: Yet this imperial enterprise had Shenyuan as its head.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the imperial enterprise truly began with Emperor Shenyuan.

sentences.zh: 案神元、晉武，往來和好。

translations.literal: Examining Shenyuan and Jin Wu, they exchanged visits in friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenyuan and Emperor Wu of Jin maintained cordial relations.

sentences.zh: 至于桓、穆，洛京破亡。

translations.literal: Reaching Huan and Mu, the Luoyang capital was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: By the reigns of Emperors Huan and Mu, Luoyang had fallen.

sentences.zh: 二帝志摧聰、勒，思存晉氏，每助劉琨，申威并冀。

translations.literal: The two emperors resolved to break Cong and Le, thinking to preserve the Jin house, always aiding Liu Kun and displaying might in Bing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: These two rulers aimed to smash Liu Cong and Shi Le, resolved to preserve the Jin dynasty, repeatedly aided Liu Kun, and projected power across Bing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 是以晉室銜扶救之仁，越石深代王之請。

translations.literal: Therefore the Jin house carried the benevolence of rescue and support, and Yue Shi deeply felt the Prince of Dai's entreaty.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Jin court acknowledged the grace of Tuoba rescue, and Liu Kun acknowledged the deep obligation owed to the Prince of Dai.

sentences.zh: 平文、太祖，抗衡苻石，終平燕氏，大造中區。

translations.literal: Emperors Wen and Taizu resisted Fu and Shi, finally pacified the Murong house, [19] and greatly created the Central region.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Wen and Taizu stood against Fu Jian and Shi Hu, finally conquered the Murong Yan, [19] and rebuilt the Central Domain.

sentences.zh: 則是司馬祚終於郟鄏，而元氏受命於雲代。

translations.literal: Thus the Sima fortune ended at Jia and Ruo, while the Yuan clan received the mandate at Yun and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: The Sima line ended in the Zhou heartland, while the Yuan clan received the Mandate in Yun and Dai.

sentences.zh: 蓋自周之滅及漢正號，幾六十年，著符尚赤。

translations.literal: From Zhou's extinction until Han's proper title, nearly sixty years passed, and the tally favored red.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhou's fall until Han claimed the throne, nearly sixty years elapsed—and the omens favored red.

sentences.zh: 後雖張、賈殊議，暫疑而卒從火德，以繼周氏。

translations.literal: Later though Zhang and Jia disputed variously, after brief doubt they ultimately followed Fire Virtue to succeed the Zhou clan.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhang Cang and Jia Yi later disagreed, Han soon settled on Fire Virtue as successor to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 排虐嬴以比共工，蔑暴項而同吳廣。

translations.literal: Rejecting cruel Ying and comparing to Gong Gong; scorning tyrannical Xiang and equaling Wu Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Han rejected the Qin tyrant Ying as Gong Gong had been rejected, and disdained the brutal Xiang Yu as it had Wu Guang.

sentences.zh: 近蠲謬偽，遠即神正，若此之明也。

translations.literal: Near, it cleared out error and falsity; far, it accorded with divine orthodoxy—such is its clarity.
translations.idiomatic: In the near term it cast off false claimants; in principle it aligned with Heaven's true succession—so lucid a logic.

sentences.zh: 寧使白蛇徒斬，雕雲空結哉！

translations.literal: Better to let the white serpent be cut in vain and the carved cloud be tied for nothing!
translations.idiomatic: Surely one would rather see the white serpent slashed to no purpose and the carved cloud sign come to nothing!

sentences.zh: 自有晉傾淪，暨登國肇號，亦幾六十餘載，物色旗幟，率多從黑。

translations.literal: From Jin's collapse until the founding of the state at Dengguo, also nearly sixty-odd years passed, and colors of goods, banners, and flags mostly followed black.
translations.idiomatic: From Jin's fall to the founding of our dynasty at Dengguo, again nearly sixty years passed—and colors, banners, and flags largely favored black.

sentences.zh: 是又自然合應，玄同漢始。

translations.literal: This again naturally accorded in response; dark [black] matched Han's beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Here again nature offered its own confirmation—black, like the Han at its founding.

sentences.zh: 且秦并天下，革創法度，漢仍其制，少所變易。

translations.literal: Moreover Qin united the realm and newly fashioned laws and institutions; Han continued its system with little change.
translations.idiomatic: Qin unified the realm and forged its institutions; Han largely kept them with few alterations.

sentences.zh: 猶仰推五運，竟踵隆姬。

translations.literal: Still it looked up to reckon the Five Cycles and ultimately followed flourishing Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Han still traced the Five Cycles back through time and ultimately claimed succession from flourishing Zhou.

sentences.zh: 而況劉、石、苻、燕，世業促褊，綱紀弗立。

translations.literal: How much more Liu, Shi, Fu, and Yan—their dynastic enterprises were brief and narrow, their guiding cords were not established.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Liu, Shi, Fu, and Yan dynasties were passing and petty, their institutions never firmly established.

sentences.zh: 魏接其弊，自有彝典，豈可異漢之承木，捨晉而為土耶？

translations.literal: Wei received their decay and has its own canonical rites—how could it differ from Han's inheriting Wood, discard Jin, and be Earth?
translations.idiomatic: Wei inherited their ruin and possesses its own sacred canon—how could it break with Han's precedent of succeeding Zhou's Wood to become Fire, abandon Jin, and declare Earth Virtue?

sentences.zh: 夫皇統崇極，承運至重，必當推恊天緒，考審王次，不可雜以僭竊，參之強狡。

translations.literal: Imperial lineage at the supreme height—inheriting fortune is supremely weighty; one must surely accord with Heaven's thread, examine and review the order of kings, and cannot mix in usurping thefts or consult with violent cunning.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial succession is a matter of the highest gravity; one must align with Heaven's plan and soberly weigh the true order of kings—not mingle with usurpers or heed the strong and the cunning.

sentences.zh: 神元既晉武同世，桓、穆與懷、愍接時。

translations.literal: Shenyuan was of the same era as Jin Wu; Huan and Mu connected in time with Huai and Min.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenyuan was contemporaneous with Emperor Wu of Jin; Emperors Huan and Mu were contemporaneous with Emperors Huai and Min.

sentences.zh: 晉室之淪，平文始大，廟號太祖，抑亦有由。

translations.literal: The Jin house's collapse—Wen's rise began greatly; the temple title Grand Ancestor indeed has its grounds.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin dynasty fell, Emperor Wen first raised Great Wei's fortunes; that his temple name is Grand Ancestor is not without reason.

sentences.zh: 紹晉定德，孰曰不可，而欲次茲偽僭，豈非惑乎？

translations.literal: Continuing Jin and fixing virtue—who says it cannot be done? Yet to wish to rank these false usurpers in sequence—is this not confusion?
translations.idiomatic: To succeed Jin and fix our elemental virtue—who would deny it? To place these illegitimate interlopers in the line of succession—is that not folly?

sentences.zh: 臣所以慺慺惜之，唯垂察納。」

translations.literal: Therefore your ministers earnestly regret this and only ask that you examine and accept."
translations.idiomatic: This is why your servants plead earnestly and beg only that Your Majesty weigh and approve our view."

sentences.zh: 詔令羣官議之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the assembled officials to debate it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commanded all officials to debate the matter.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月，侍中、司空、長樂王穆亮，侍中、尚書左僕射、平原王陸叡，侍中、吏部尚書、中山王王元孫，侍中、尚書、駙馬都尉、南平王馮誕，散騎常侍、都曹尚書、新泰侯游明根，[20]散騎常侍、南部令鄧侍祖，秘書中散李愷，尚書左丞郭祚，右丞、霸城子衞慶，中書侍郎封琳，中書郎、泰昌子崔挺，中書侍郎賈元壽等言：「臣等受敕共議中書監高閭、秘書丞李彪等二人所議皇魏行次。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year, Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, Prince of Changle Mu Liang; Palace Attendant, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, Prince of Pingyuan Lu Rui; Palace Attendant, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Prince of Zhongshan Wang Yuansun; Palace Attendant, Secretary, Commandant of the Horse, Prince of Nanping Feng Dan; Attendant-in-Regular Service, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Marquis of Xintai You Minggen, [20] Attendant-in-Regular Service, Director of the Southern Bureau Deng Shizu; Secretariat Secretary Li Kai; Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat Guo Zuo; Right Assistant Director, Viscount of Bacheng Wei Qing; Secretariat Gentleman Feng Lin; Secretariat Gentleman, Viscount of Taichang Cui Ting; Secretariat Gentleman Jia Yuanshou, and others said: "We have received command jointly to debate the imperial Wei's dynastic succession as argued by Secretariat Director Gao Lu and Secretariat Assistant Li Biao and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifteenth year, Mu Liang, Prince of Changle, Palace Attendant and Minister of Works; Lu Rui, Prince of Pingyuan, Palace Attendant and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat; Wang Yuansun, Prince of Zhongshan, Palace Attendant and Director of Personnel; Feng Dan, Prince of Nanping, Palace Attendant and Commandant of the Horse; You Minggen, Marquis of Xintai, Attendant-in-Regular Service and Director of the Department of State Affairs; [20] and Deng Shizu, Li Kai, Guo Zuo, Wei Qing, Feng Lin, Cui Ting, Jia Yuanshou, and others memorialized: "We have been ordered to deliberate the succession sequence proposed by Gao Lu, Li Biao, and their colleagues for Imperial Wei.

sentences.zh: 尚書高閭以石承晉為水德，以燕承石為木德，以秦承燕為火德，大魏次秦為土德，皆以地據中夏，以為得統之徵。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Gao Lu took Shi succeeding Jin as Water Virtue, Yan succeeding Shi as Wood Virtue, Qin succeeding Yan as Fire Virtue, and Great Wei following Qin as Earth Virtue—all on the grounds of holding the Central Xia, taken as signs of obtaining the succession.
translations.idiomatic: Director Gao Lu held that Later Zhao succeeded Jin as Water, Yan succeeded Zhao as Wood, Former Qin succeeded Yan as Fire, and Great Wei followed Qin as Earth—each on grounds of holding the Central Plains as proof of legitimate succession.

sentences.zh: 皇魏建號，事接秦末，晉既滅亡，天命在我。

translations.literal: Imperial Wei established its title; affairs joined Qin's end; Jin was already extinguished—the Mandate of Heaven is with us.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Wei rose at the fall of Former Qin; Jin had already perished—and Heaven's mandate rested with us.

sentences.zh: 故因中原有寄，即而承之。

translations.literal: Therefore, because the Central Plains had a resting place, they immediately succeeded it.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, because legitimacy had a haven in the Central Plains, Wei took up that succession directly.

sentences.zh: 彪等據神元皇帝與晉武並時，桓、穆二帝，仍修舊好。

translations.literal: Biao and others rely on Emperor Shenyuan being contemporary with Jin Wu, and the two emperors Huan and Mu still maintaining the former friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Li Biao and his allies argue that Emperor Shenyuan was contemporary with Emperor Wu of Jin, and that Emperors Huan and Mu continued the old alliance.

sentences.zh: 始自平文，逮于太祖，抗衡秦、趙，終平慕容。

translations.literal: Beginning from Wen, reaching Taizu, they resisted Qin and Zhao and finally pacified Murong.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Wen through Emperor Taizu, they stood against Former Qin and Later Zhao and finally overthrew the Murong Yan.

sentences.zh: 晉祚終於秦方，大魏興於雲朔。

translations.literal: Jin's fortune ended in Qin's territory; Great Wei rose in Yun and Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's mandate ended in the Qin heartland, while Great Wei arose in the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 據漢棄秦承周之義，以皇魏承晉為水德。

translations.literal: Relying on Han's principle of abandoning Qin to succeed Zhou, they take Imperial Wei succeeding Jin as Water Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Following Han's precedent of rejecting Qin to succeed Zhou, they would make Imperial Wei succeed Jin as Water Virtue.

sentences.zh: 二家之論，大略如此。

translations.literal: The arguments of the two factions are roughly thus.
translations.idiomatic: In broad outline, the two positions are as stated.

sentences.zh: 臣等謹共參論，伏惟皇魏世王玄朔，下迄魏、晉，趙、秦、二燕雖地據中華，德祚微淺，並獲推敍，於理未愜。

translations.literal: Your ministers respectfully join in discussion: bowing in reverence, Imperial Wei has ruled the dark north for generations; down to Wei, Jin, Zhao, Qin, and the two Yan—though they held territory in the Central States, their virtue and fortune were slight and shallow, yet all would receive promotion in the sequence—in principle this is unsatisfactory.
translations.idiomatic: We have deliberated together and conclude: though Imperial Wei has long ruled the north, to elevate Wei, Jin, Zhao, Qin, and both Yan states in the succession—despite their shallow virtue and brief reigns, solely because they held Chinese soil—satisfies neither reason nor precedent.

sentences.zh: 又國家積德修長，道光萬載。

translations.literal: Moreover the state's accumulated virtue is long-cultivated, its Way shining for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's accumulated virtue is deep and enduring; its brilliance should shine across ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 彪等職主東觀，詳究圖史，所據之理，其致難奪。

translations.literal: Biao and others' office presides over the Eastern Pavilion; they have examined maps and histories in detail—the principles they rely on are hard to overturn.
translations.idiomatic: Li Biao and his colleagues, keepers of the Eastern Archives, have scrutinized historical records—and the logic they invoke is formidable.

sentences.zh: 今欲從彪等所議，宜承晉為水德。」

translations.literal: Now wishing to follow Biao and others' proposal, one ought to succeed Jin as Water Virtue."
translations.idiomatic: We therefore favor Li Biao's position: Imperial Wei should succeed Jin as Water Virtue."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「越近承遠，情所未安。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Overleaping the near to inherit the distant—in feeling this is not yet settled.
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied: "To skip what is near and claim what is far does not sit well with me.

sentences.zh: 然考次推時，頗亦難繼。

translations.literal: Yet examining order and reckoning the age, it is indeed hard to continue.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to trace the sequence through time is also hard to sustain.

sentences.zh: 朝賢所議，豈朕能有違奪。

translations.literal: What the court worthies debated—how could I have the power to oppose or withhold?
translations.idiomatic: When the court worthies have spoken, how could I overrule them?

sentences.zh: 便可依為水德，祖申臘辰。」

translations.literal: Let it be done according to Water Virtue, with Shen and La months as ancestral sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: Let Water Virtue stand, with the Shen and twelfth-month sacrifices as our ancestral rite."

sentences.zh: 四月，經始明堂，改營太廟。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, work began on the Bright Hall and the Grand Ancestral Temple was rebuilt.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month work began on the Bright Hall and the Grand Temple was reconstructed.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「祖有功，宗有德，自非功德厚者，不得擅祖宗之名，居二祧之廟。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Ancestors have merit, and temple lords have virtue—unless merit and virtue are substantial, one may not arbitrarily take the names of ancestor or temple lord or occupy the two zhao shrines.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "'Ancestor' honors achievement; 'Temple Lord' honors virtue—none but those of the greatest merit and virtue may bear those titles or hold places in the two eternal shrines.

sentences.zh: 仰惟先朝舊事，舛駁不同，難以取準。

translations.literal: Looking up to consider former court precedents, they are confused and contradictory, hard to take as standard.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing earlier court practice, the precedents are tangled and inconsistent—no reliable standard emerges.

sentences.zh: 今將述遵先志，具詳禮典，宜制祖宗之號，定將來之法。

translations.literal: Now we shall narrate and follow former intent, fully detailing the ritual canon; it is fitting to establish the titles of ancestor and temple lord and fix the law for the future.
translations.idiomatic: We must now follow our forebears' intent, set out the ritual code fully, fix the titles of Ancestor and Temple Lord, and establish the rule for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 烈祖有創基之功，世祖有開拓之德，宜為祖宗，百世不遷。

translations.literal: Illustrious Ancestor had the achievement of founding the base; World Ancestor had the virtue of opening and expanding—they should be ancestor and temple lord, not moved for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Illustrious Ancestor founded the realm; World Ancestor expanded it—both deserve the titles of Ancestor and Temple Lord, immovable for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 而遠祖平文功未多於昭成，然廟號為太祖；

translations.literal: Yet distant ancestor Wen's achievements were not much greater than Zhaocheng's, yet his temple title was Grand Ancestor;
translations.idiomatic: Yet remote ancestor Wen accomplished no more than Zhaocheng—yet bore the temple title Grand Ancestor;

sentences.zh: 道武建業之勳，高於平文，廟號為烈祖。

translations.literal: Daowu's achievements in establishing the enterprise were higher than Wen's, yet his temple title was Illustrious Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: while Daowu, whose founding achievements surpassed Wen's, received only Illustrious Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 比功校德，以為未允。

translations.literal: Comparing achievement and weighing virtue, we hold this unsatisfactory.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing service against merit, we find this unsatisfactory.

sentences.zh: 朕今奉尊道武為太祖，與顯祖為二祧，餘者以次而遷。

translations.literal: We now respectfully honor Daowu as Grand Ancestor, with Xianzu as the two zhao, and the rest moved in successive order.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore honor Daowu as Grand Ancestor and Xianzu as the second eternal shrine; the remainder will shift down in order.

sentences.zh: 平文既遷，廟唯有六，始今七廟，一則無主。

translations.literal: Once Wen is moved, the temple will have only six; beginning now with seven temples, one will have no occupant.
translations.idiomatic: With Wen removed, the temple holds only six shrines; instituting seven leaves one without a lord.

sentences.zh: 唯當朕躬此事，亦臣子所難言。

translations.literal: Only when it falls to our own person in this matter—it is also what ministers and sons find hard to speak of.
translations.idiomatic: Only when my own death supplies the seventh seat—and that is what no subject dares broach.

sentences.zh: 夫生必有終，人之常理。

translations.literal: Birth must have an end—the constant principle of humanity.
translations.idiomatic: All who live must die; that is human nature.

sentences.zh: 朕以不德，忝承洪緒，若宗廟之靈，獲全首領以沒于地，為昭穆之次，心願畢矣。

translations.literal: We, lacking virtue, unworthily inherit the great line; if the ancestral temple spirits grant us to keep our head complete and die upon the earth, placed in the zhao-mu order, our heart's wish would be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Lacking virtue, I unworthily bear this great line. If the spirits of the ancestral temple grant me a peaceful death and a place in the proper zhao-mu order, my heart's desire will be fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 必不可豫，設可垂之文，示後必令遷之。」

translations.literal: It absolutely cannot be done in advance; if we set down a lasting text showing future generations, we must afterward order that it be moved."
translations.idiomatic: This cannot be decided prematurely; if I commit it to writing for posterity, I must afterward command that my shrine be moved."

sentences.zh: 司空公、長樂王穆亮等奏言：「升平之會，事在於今。

translations.literal: Minister of Works, Duke, Prince of Changle Mu Liang and others memorialized: "The occasion of ascending peace—the matter is in the present.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Liang, Minister of Works and Prince of Changle, and his colleagues memorialized: "The moment of peace and proper order is now.

sentences.zh: 推功考德，實如明旨。

translations.literal: Weighing achievement and examining virtue, it is truly as in the clarified intent.
translations.idiomatic: Your assessment of merit and virtue is entirely correct.

sentences.zh: 但七廟之祀，備行日久，無宜闕一，虛有所待。

translations.literal: But the seven-temple sacrifices have long been fully performed; it is not fitting to lack one and leave a vacancy in waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the seven-shrine ritual has long been complete; it is unfitting to leave one seat empty in indefinite waiting.

sentences.zh: 臣等愚謂，依先尊祀，可垂文示後。

translations.literal: Your ministers foolishly hold that following the former honored sacrifices, a lasting text may be shown to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly propose that the court maintain the present honors for now and commit the arrangement to written precedent.

sentences.zh: 理衷如此，不敢不言。」

translations.literal: Reason and inward conviction are thus—we dare not fail to speak."
translations.idiomatic: This is our honest view, and we dare not withhold it."

sentences.zh: 詔曰「理或如此。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Reason may be thus.
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied: "That reasoning may stand.

sentences.zh: 比有間隙，當為文相示」。

translations.literal: When there is leisure in the meantime, we shall make a text and show each other."
translations.idiomatic: When time permits, I will set it down in writing for you."

sentences.zh: 八月壬辰，詔郡國有時果可薦者，並送京師以供廟饗。

translations.literal: On renchen day of the eighth month, an edict ordered that commanderies and kingdoms with seasonal fruits fit for offering should all send them to the capital for temple feasts.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day of the eighth month, an edict commanded that wherever seasonal fruit suitable for offering could be obtained, it should be sent to the capital for ancestral temple rites.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「禮云自外至者，無主不立。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "Ritual says: what comes from without—without a lord it is not established.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict declared: "The Rites say: What comes from without cannot be established without a lord.

sentences.zh: 先朝以來，以正月吉日，於朝廷設幕，中置松栢樹，設五帝坐。

translations.literal: Since the former court, on an auspicious day of the first month, a canopy was set up at court, with pine and cypress placed in the center and seats for the Five Emperors established.
translations.idiomatic: Former courts observed an auspicious day in the first month by erecting a canopy at court, setting pine and cypress at its center, and arranging seats for the Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 此既無可祖配，揆之古典，實無所取，可去此祀。

translations.literal: This has no ancestor with whom to pair; measured against classical antiquity, it truly has nothing worth taking—this sacrifice may be removed.
translations.idiomatic: No ancestral spirit can be paired with this rite; by classical precedent it serves no purpose—this ceremony should be abolished.

sentences.zh: 又探策之祭，既非禮典，可悉罷之。」

translations.literal: Also, the sacrifice of probing the divination stalks, since it is not in the ritual canon, may entirely be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: The rite of probing the divination stalks, moreover, is no part of the canonical ritual—it should be abolished altogether."

sentences.zh: 戊午詔曰：「國家自先朝以來，饗祀諸神，凡有一千二百餘處。

translations.literal: On the wuwu day an edict said: "Since the former court, feasts and sacrifices to the various spirits have totaled more than twelve hundred sites.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day an edict declared: "Since earlier reigns the state has maintained sacrificial feasts to the spirits at more than twelve hundred shrines.

sentences.zh: 今欲減省羣祀，務從簡約。

translations.literal: Now we wish to reduce and simplify collective sacrifices, striving for simplicity and austerity.
translations.idiomatic: We now intend to cut back the multitude of sacrifices and keep them as simple as possible.

sentences.zh: 昔漢高之初，所祀眾神及寢廟不少今日。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Emperor Gaozu of Han, the spirits worshipped and the sleeping temples were not few compared with today.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Han under Gaozu, the gods honored and the ancestral sleeping temples were scarcely fewer than today's.

sentences.zh: 至于元、成之際，匡衡執論，乃得減省。

translations.literal: By the reigns of Yuanshi and Chengdi, Kuang Heng held to his arguments, and only then was reduction achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the Yuanshi and Chengdi reigns, when Kuang Heng pressed his case, was any real reduction achieved.

sentences.zh: 後至光武之世，禮儀始備，饗祀有序。

translations.literal: Later, by the era of Emperor Guangwu, ritual propriety was first made complete and sacrificial feasts were ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Later, under Emperor Guangwu, ritual was at last fully established and sacrificial worship was put in proper order.

sentences.zh: 凡祭不欲數，數則黷，黷則不敬。

translations.literal: In general, sacrifices should not be frequent; if frequent they become profane, and if profane they lack reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice should not be performed too often; frequency breeds profanation, and profanation breeds irreverence.

sentences.zh: 神聰明正直，不待煩祀也。」

translations.literal: The spirits are discerning, upright, and honest—they do not await tedious sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: The spirits are discerning and upright; they have no need of excessive offerings."

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「明堂、太廟，並祀祖宗，配祭配享，於斯備矣。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "The Bright Hall and Grand Ancestral Temple together worship the ancestors; paired sacrifice and enshrined offerings are here complete.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict stated: "At the Bright Hall and Grand Ancestral Temple the ancestors are worshipped together; paired offerings and enshrined companions are fully provided for there.

sentences.zh: 白登、崞山、雞鳴山廟唯遣有司行事。

translations.literal: The temples at Baideng, Guoshan, and Jimingshan need only have the officials in charge perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the temples of Baideng, Guoshan, and Jimingshan, let the responsible officials alone carry out the ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 馮宣王誕生先后，復因在官長安，立廟宜異常等。

translations.literal: Prince Xuan of Feng was born to the empress consort, and moreover because the court was at Chang'an, the temple established for him should be of exceptional rank.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xuan of Feng was born to the empress consort, and since the court then resided at Chang'an, the shrine raised for him should be accorded exceptional standing.

sentences.zh: 可敕雍州，以時供祭。」

translations.literal: Yong Province may be ordered to supply sacrifices at the proper seasons."
translations.idiomatic: Yong Province should be instructed to furnish offerings at the appointed seasons."

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「先恒有水火之神四十餘名，及城北星神。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "Formerly there were constantly more than forty water and fire spirits, as well as the Star Spirit north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict noted: "Formerly more than forty spirits of water and fire were regularly honored, along with the Star Spirit north of the city.

sentences.zh: 今圓丘之下，既祭風伯、雨師、司中、司命，明堂祭門、戶、井、竈、中霤，每神皆有。

translations.literal: Now beneath the Round Mound the Earl of Wind, Master of Rain, Director of the Center, and Director of Fate are already sacrificed to; at the Bright Hall Gate, Household, Well, Stove, and Central Drain are sacrificed to—each spirit is already provided for.
translations.idiomatic: At the Round Mound the Earl of Wind, Master of Rain, Director of the Center, and Director of Fate are already worshipped; at the Bright Hall the Gate, Household, Well, Stove, and Central Drain each have their own rite—every one of these spirits is already accounted for.

sentences.zh: 此四十神計不須立，悉可罷之。」

translations.literal: These forty spirits, reckoned together, need not be established; all may be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: These forty deities need not be maintained at all and may be abolished entirely."

sentences.zh: 甲寅，集羣官，詔曰：「近論朝日夕月，皆欲以二分之日，於東西郊行禮。

translations.literal: On the jiayin day the assembled officials were gathered and an edict said: "Recently in discussion of the morning sun and evening moon rites, all wished to perform the ceremony at the eastern and western suburbs on the days of the equinoxes.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day the officials were assembled and an edict declared: "In recent debate over the morning-sun and evening-moon ceremonies, all proposed holding them at the eastern and western suburbs on the equinox days.

sentences.zh: 然月有餘閏，行無常準。

translations.literal: Yet the moon has surplus and intercalary months; its movements have no fixed standard.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the moon has extra and intercalary days, and its course follows no fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 若一依分日，或值月出於東，而行禮於西，尋情即理，不可施行。

translations.literal: If one rigidly followed the equinox days, perhaps the moon would rise in the east while the rite was performed in the west—weighing feeling and principle, this cannot be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: If the equinox alone were followed, the moon might rise in the east while the rite was performed in the west; judged by both sentiment and reason, such a practice cannot be adopted.

sentences.zh: 昔秘書監薛謂等嘗論此事，以為朝日以朔，夕月以朏。

translations.literal: Formerly Director of the Secretariat Xue Wei and others once discussed this matter, holding that the morning sun [rite] should be on the new moon and the evening moon [rite] on the crescent moon.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Xue Wei, Director of the Secretariat, and others debated this question and held that the morning-sun rite should fall on the new moon and the evening-moon rite on the crescent.

sentences.zh: 卿等意謂朔朏二分，何者為是？」

translations.literal: What do you consider correct—the new moon and crescent, or the equinoxes?"
translations.idiomatic: Which do you deem correct—the new moon and crescent, or the equinoxes?"

sentences.zh: 尚書游明根對曰「考案舊式，推校眾議，宜從朏月」。

translations.literal: Minister You Minggen replied: "Examining established precedents and weighing the collective discussion, the crescent-moon [rule] should be followed."
translations.idiomatic: Minister You Minggen answered: "After reviewing old precedents and weighing the general opinion, the crescent-moon rule should be adopted."

sentences.zh: 十一月己未朔，帝釋禫祭於太和廟。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eleventh month, jimei, the Emperor ended the mourning seclusion and sacrificed at the Taihe Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the new-moon day jimei of the eleventh month, the Emperor ended mourning seclusion and offered sacrifice at the Taihe Temple.

sentences.zh: 帝衮冕，與祭者朝服。

translations.literal: The Emperor wore the ceremonial robe and cap; those joining the sacrifice wore court dress.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wore full ceremonial regalia; those attending the sacrifice wore court dress.

sentences.zh: 既而帝冠黑介幘，素紗深衣，拜山陵而還宮。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Emperor capped himself with a black kerchief and wore plain gauze deep robes, paid respects at the imperial tombs, and returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Emperor put on a black kerchief cap and plain gauze deep robes, paid homage at the imperial tombs, and returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 庚申，帝親省齊宮冠服及郊祀俎豆。

translations.literal: On gengshen day the Emperor personally inspected the fasting-palace caps and robes and the suburban sacrifice vessels and stands.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day the Emperor personally examined the fasting-palace vestments and the vessels and stands for the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 癸亥冬至，將祭圓丘，帝衮冕劍舄，侍臣朝服。

translations.literal: On the guihai day, the winter solstice, about to sacrifice at the Round Mound, the Emperor wore ceremonial robe and cap, sword and shoes; attendant ministers wore court dress.
translations.idiomatic: On the winter solstice, guihai day, as he prepared to sacrifice at the Round Mound, the Emperor wore ceremonial robes, sword, and court shoes, and his attendants wore court dress.

sentences.zh: 辭太和廟，之圓丘，升祭柴燎，遂祀明堂，大合。

translations.literal: He took leave of the Taihe Temple, went to the Round Mound, ascended and offered the burnt sacrifice, then worshipped at the Bright Hall in a great assembly.
translations.idiomatic: He took leave at the Taihe Temple, proceeded to the Round Mound, ascended and burned the offering, then worshipped at the Bright Hall in a grand ceremony.

sentences.zh: 既而還之太和廟，乃入。

translations.literal: Thereupon returning to the Taihe Temple, he then entered.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned to the Taihe Temple before entering the palace.

sentences.zh: 甲子，帝衮冕辭太和廟，臨太華殿，朝羣官。

translations.literal: On jiazi day the Emperor, in ceremonial robe and cap, took leave of the Taihe Temple, proceeded to the Taihua Hall, and held court with the assembled officials.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day, in full ceremonial dress, the Emperor took leave at the Taihe Temple, entered the Taihua Hall, and held audience with the officials.

sentences.zh: 既而帝冠通天，絳紗袍，臨饗禮。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Emperor capped himself with the tongtian cap and wore a crimson gauze robe, presiding over the feast ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He then donned the tongtian cap and crimson gauze robe and presided over the feast ceremony.

sentences.zh: 帝感慕，樂懸而不作。

translations.literal: The Emperor, moved with longing, had the suspended bells and chimes hung but not struck.
translations.idiomatic: Overcome with grief and longing, the Emperor had the bells and chimes hung but not played.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，遷廟，陳列冕服，帝躬省之。

translations.literal: On dingmao day, during the temple transfer, the caps and robes were displayed and the Emperor personally inspected them.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day, during the transfer of the ancestral temple, the ceremonial caps and robes were laid out and the Emperor inspected them in person.

sentences.zh: 既而帝衮冕，辭太和廟，之太廟，百官陪從。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Emperor, in ceremonial robe and cap, took leave of the Taihe Temple and went to the Grand Ancestral Temple, with the hundred officials accompanying.
translations.idiomatic: Then, in full ceremonial dress, the Emperor took leave at the Taihe Temple and proceeded to the Grand Ancestral Temple, attended by the officials.

sentences.zh: 奉神主於齋車，至新廟。

translations.literal: The spirit tablets were carried on the fasting carriage to the new temple.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit tablets were borne on the fasting carriage to the new temple.

sentences.zh: 有司升神主於太廟，諸王侯牧守、四海蕃附，各以其職來祭。

translations.literal: The officials raised the spirit tablets in the Grand Ancestral Temple; princes, marquises, governors, and frontier dependents from all directions came to sacrifice according to their offices.
translations.idiomatic: The officials installed the spirit tablets in the Grand Ancestral Temple, and princes, marquises, governors, and tributaries from all quarters came to offer sacrifice according to their rank.

sentences.zh: 十六年正月戊午，詔曰：「夫四時享祀，人子常道。

translations.literal: On the wuwu day of the first month of the sixteenth year, an edict said: "Seasonal offerings through the four seasons are the constant duty of a son.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day of the first month of the sixteenth year, an edict declared: "Seasonal offerings are the constant obligation of a filial son.

sentences.zh: 然祭薦之禮，貴賤不同。

translations.literal: Yet the ritual of offering sacrifice differs between noble and humble.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the rites of sacrificial offering differ according to rank.

sentences.zh: 故有邑之君，祭以首時，無田之士，薦以仲月。

translations.literal: Hence the lord with a fief sacrifices at the first season; the gentleman without fields offers at the middle month.
translations.idiomatic: A lord with a fief sacrifices at the first season; a gentleman without land offers in the middle month.

sentences.zh: 況七廟之重，而用中節者哉！

translations.literal: How much more the weight of the seven temples—yet use the middle season!
translations.idiomatic: How much less, then, should the weight of the seven temples be served by a middle-season rite!

sentences.zh: 自頃蒸嘗之禮，頗違舊義。

translations.literal: Recently the winter and autumn offerings have deviated considerably from the old meaning.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times the winter and autumn offerings have departed considerably from the old meaning.

sentences.zh: 今將仰遵遠式，以此孟月，犆礿於太廟。

translations.literal: Now we shall look up and follow the distant models; in this first month of spring, perform the special yue offering at the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: We shall now look back to ancient precedent and, in this first month of spring, perform the special yue offering at the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 但朝典初改，眾務殷湊，無遑齋潔，遂及於今。

translations.literal: But the court regulations were just revised, and duties piled pressing—there was no leisure for fasting and purification, and so it has reached today.
translations.idiomatic: But the court rites had only just been revised, affairs pressed in from every side, and there was no time for fasting and purification—thus matters have reached the present day.

sentences.zh: 又接神饗祖，必須擇日。

translations.literal: Moreover, receiving the spirits and feasting the ancestors requires choosing a day.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, receiving the spirits and feasting the ancestors requires that a day be chosen.

sentences.zh: 今禮律未宣，有司或不知此。

translations.literal: Now the ritual statutes have not been promulgated; officials perhaps do not know this.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual statutes have not yet been announced, and officials may not know this.

sentences.zh: 可敕太常令剋日以聞。」

translations.literal: The Director of Imperial Worship may be ordered to fix a day and report."
translations.idiomatic: Let the Director of Imperial Worship be instructed to fix a day and report back."

sentences.zh: 二月丁酉，詔曰：「夫崇聖祀德，遠代之通典；

translations.literal: On the dingyou day of the second month, an edict said: "Honoring sages and worshipping virtue are universal norms of distant ages;
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day of the second month, an edict declared: "Honoring sages and worshipping the virtuous is a universal practice of antiquity;

sentences.zh: 秩□□□，中古之近規。

translations.literal: Rank □□□, a recent regulation of the middle antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Rank □□□ is a recent norm of the middle ages.

sentences.zh: 故三五至仁，唯德配享；

translations.literal: Hence the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, most benevolent, were enshrined only by virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, supreme in benevolence, were enshrined by virtue alone;

sentences.zh: 夏殷私己，稍用其姓。

translations.literal: Xia and Yin served their own clans and gradually used their own surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Xia and Yin favored their own kin and gradually enshrined their own clansmen.

sentences.zh: 且法施於民，祀有明典，立功垂惠，祭有恒式。

translations.literal: Moreover, when law is bestowed upon the people, sacrifice has clear statutes; when merit is established and bounty extended, offering has constant forms.
translations.idiomatic: When law is given to the people, sacrifice has clear statutes; when merit is achieved and blessings extended, offering has fixed forms.

sentences.zh: 斯乃異代同途，弈世共軌。

translations.literal: This is the same path across different ages, the common track through successive generations.
translations.idiomatic: Different ages have followed the same path; generation after generation has kept to the same course.

sentences.zh: 今遠遵明令，憲章舊則，比於祀令，已為決之。

translations.literal: Now, far following the enlightened command and taking the old rules as charter, compared with the sacrificial ordinances, this has already been decided.
translations.idiomatic: We now follow the enlightened edict from afar and take the old rules as our charter; as against the sacrificial ordinances, the matter has already been settled.

sentences.zh: 其孟春應祀者，頃以事殷，遂及今日。

translations.literal: Those who should be worshipped in early spring—the pressure of affairs delayed matters until today.
translations.idiomatic: Those due for worship in early spring have been delayed by pressing affairs until today.

sentences.zh: 可令仍以仲月而饗祀焉。

translations.literal: They may be ordered to feast and sacrifice still in the middle month.
translations.idiomatic: Let them be instructed to perform the feast and sacrifice in the middle month instead.

sentences.zh: 凡在祀令者，其數有五。

translations.literal: Of those on the sacrificial ordinance, the number is five.
translations.idiomatic: Those listed on the sacrificial ordinance number five in all.

sentences.zh: 帝堯樹則天之功，興巍巍之治，可祀於平陽。

translations.literal: Emperor Yao raised the merit of conforming to Heaven and brought forth lofty governance—he may be worshipped at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yao established the merit of aligning with Heaven and brought forth a lofty order of government—he may be worshipped at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 虞舜播太平之風，致無為之化，可祀於廣寧。

translations.literal: Yu-Shun spread the breeze of great peace and achieved transformation through non-action—he may be worshipped at Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: Yu-Shun spread the spirit of great peace and achieved rule through non-action—he may be worshipped at Guangning.

sentences.zh: 夏禹禦洪水之災，建天下之利，可祀於安邑。

translations.literal: Yu of Xia stemmed the disaster of great floods and established benefits for all under Heaven—he may be worshipped at Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu of Xia checked the calamity of the great flood and built benefits for all under Heaven—he may be worshipped at Anyi.

sentences.zh: 周文公制禮作樂，垂範萬葉，可祀於洛陽。

translations.literal: Duke Wen of Zhou established ritual and made music, leaving a model for ten thousand generations—he may be worshipped at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen of Zhou fashioned ritual and music, leaving a model for ten thousand generations—he may be worshipped at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 其宣尼之廟，已於中省，當別敕有司。

translations.literal: As for the temple of Confucius, it has already been set at the Directorate—[21] separate orders should be issued to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: As for the temple of Confucius, it has already been established at the Directorate;[21] separate orders should be issued to the responsible officials.

sentences.zh: 饗薦之禮，自文公已上，可令當界牧守，各隨所近，攝行祀事，皆用清酌尹祭也。」

translations.literal: The feast and offering rituals, from Duke Wen upward, may have the governors of the bordering territories each according to proximity conduct the sacrificial affairs in proxy, all using pure libation and overseen sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: For the feast and offering rites from Duke Wen upward, let the governors of the nearest territories each, according to proximity, conduct the sacrifices in proxy, all using pure libation and ministerial oversight."

sentences.zh: 丙午，詔有司剋吉亥，備小駕，躬臨千畝，官別有敕。

translations.literal: On bingwu day, officials were ordered to fix an auspicious hai day, prepare the lesser imperial train, and the Emperor would personally attend the Thousand-Acre field; each office had separate orders.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day officials were ordered to choose an auspicious hai day, prepare the lesser imperial escort, and have the Emperor personally attend the Thousand-Acre field; each office received separate instructions.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，帝臨宣文堂，引儀曹尚書劉昶、鴻臚卿游明根、行儀曹事李韶，授策孔子，崇文聖之諡。

translations.literal: On guichou day the Emperor proceeded to the Xuanwen Hall, summoned Ritual Director Liu Chang, Chief of Protocol You Minggen, and Acting Ritual Director Li Shao, and conferred the edict on Confucius, elevating him with the posthumous title Wen Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou day the Emperor entered the Xuanwen Hall, summoned Liu Chang, Director of the Ritual Office, You Minggen, Chief of Protocol, and Li Shao, acting head of the Ritual Office, and conferred the edict upon Confucius, raising him with the posthumous title Wen Sheng.

sentences.zh: 於是昶等就廟行事。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chang and the others went to the temple to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Chang and the others went to the temple to carry out the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 既而，帝齋中書省，親拜祭於廟。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Emperor fasted at the Secretariat and personally bowed in sacrifice at the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Emperor fasted at the Secretariat and personally bowed in sacrifice at the temple.

sentences.zh: 九月甲寅朔，大享於明堂，祀文明太后於玄室，帝親為之詞。

translations.literal: On the first day of the ninth month, jiayin, a grand feast was held at the Bright Hall; Empress Dowager Wenming was sacrificed to in the Mysterious Chamber, and the Emperor personally composed the prayer.
translations.idiomatic: On the new-moon day jiayin of the ninth month a grand feast was held at the Bright Hall; Empress Dowager Wenming was worshipped in the Mysterious Chamber, and the Emperor composed the prayer himself.

sentences.zh: 十月己亥，詔曰：「夫先王制禮，所以經綸萬代，貽法後昆。

translations.literal: On the jihai day of the tenth month, an edict said: "Former kings established ritual in order to order all generations and bequeath law to later descendants.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day of the tenth month, an edict declared: "Former kings fashioned ritual to govern all generations and bequeath law to later descendants.

sentences.zh: 至乃郊天享祖，莫不配祭，然而有節。

translations.literal: Even in suburban worship of Heaven and feasting the ancestors, all have paired sacrifice—yet there are limits.
translations.idiomatic: Even in suburban worship of Heaven and feasting the ancestors, all have paired offerings—yet there are limits.

sentences.zh: 白登廟者，有為而興，昭穆不次。

translations.literal: The Baideng Temple was raised by circumstances; the zhao and mu order is irregular.
translations.idiomatic: The Baideng Temple arose from circumstances; the zhao and mu order there is irregular.

sentences.zh: 故太祖有三層之宇，已降無方丈之室。
