translations.literal: Hence the Grand Ancestor has a hall of three tiers, while those below have no ten-foot-square chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Grand Ancestor has a hall of three stories, while those below have no proper chamber at all.

sentences.zh: [22]又常用季秋，躬駕展虔，祀禮或有褻慢之失，嘉樂頗涉野合之譏。

translations.literal: [22] Moreover it was customary in late autumn for the Emperor personally to drive forth in reverence; in the sacrificial rites there were sometimes lapses of disrespect, and the fine music drew reproach verging on indiscriminate union.
translations.idiomatic: [22] Moreover it was customary in late autumn for the Emperor to go in person in reverence; the sacrificial rites sometimes lapsed into disrespect, and the fine music invited criticism verging on impropriety.

sentences.zh: 今授衣之旦，享祭明堂；

translations.literal: Now on the day of receiving garments, sacrifice and feast at the Bright Hall;
translations.idiomatic: Now, on the day of receiving winter garments, sacrifice and feast at the Bright Hall;

sentences.zh: 玄冬之始，奉烝太廟。

translations.literal: at the beginning of dark winter, present the winter offering at the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: at the start of deep winter, present the winter offering at the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 若復致齋白登，便為一月再駕，事成褻瀆。

translations.literal: If one again fasts at Baideng, it would mean the imperial train twice in one month—the affair would become profane.
translations.idiomatic: If fasting at Baideng were added again, the imperial train would go forth twice in one month, and the rite would become profane.

sentences.zh: 回詳二理，謂宜省一。

translations.literal: Turning back and examining the two principles, one should be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing the two practices together, one of them should be eliminated.

sentences.zh: 白登之高，未若九室之美；

translations.literal: The height of Baideng is not like the beauty of the Nine Chambers;
translations.idiomatic: The height of Baideng cannot compare with the splendor of the Nine Chambers;

sentences.zh: 幃次之華，未如清廟之盛。

translations.literal: the splendor of the canopy tent is not like the grandeur of the Pure Temple.
translations.idiomatic: the ornament of the canopy tent cannot match the majesty of the Pure Temple.

sentences.zh: 將欲廢彼東山之祀，成此二享之敬。

translations.literal: We intend to abolish that sacrifice of the Eastern Mountain and complete the reverence of these two feasts.
translations.idiomatic: We intend to abolish the sacrifice at the Eastern Mountain and complete the reverence due these two great feasts.

sentences.zh: 可具敕有司，但令內典神者，攝行祭事。

translations.literal: Officials may be fully ordered—only let those of the inner bureau who keep the spirits conduct the sacrificial affair in proxy.
translations.idiomatic: Let full orders be issued to the officials, but have only those of the inner bureau who tend the spirits conduct the sacrifice in proxy.

sentences.zh: 獻明、道武各有廟稱，可具依舊式。」

translations.literal: Xianming and Daowu each have temple designations; all may follow the old forms in full."
translations.idiomatic: Xianming and Daowu each have their temple titles; let all follow the old forms in full."

sentences.zh: 自太宗諸帝，昔無殿宇，因停之。

translations.literal: From the Taizong emperors onward, formerly there were no halls, and therefore it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: From the Taizong emperors onward there had been no halls, and so the practice was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 十八年，南巡。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, a southern tour.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the Emperor toured the south.

sentences.zh: 正月，次殷比干墓，祭以太牢。

translations.literal: In the first month, stopping at the tomb of Bi Gan of Yin, he sacrificed with the grand victim.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month, halting at the tomb of Bi Gan of Yin, he offered sacrifice with the grand victim.

sentences.zh: 三月，詔罷西郊祭天。

translations.literal: In the third month, an edict abolished heaven worship at the western suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month an edict abolished the western-suburb sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 十九年，帝南征。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, the Emperor marched south.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the Emperor marched south on campaign.

sentences.zh: 正月，車駕濟淮，命太常致祭。

translations.literal: In the first month, the imperial train crossed the Huai; the Director of Imperial Worship was ordered to conduct sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month the imperial train crossed the Huai, and the Director of Imperial Worship was ordered to perform the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 又詔祀岱岳。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered worship of Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered sacrifice at Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 二月癸亥，詔曰：「知太和廟已就，神儀靈主，宜時奉寧。

translations.literal: On the guihai day of the second month, an edict said: "Knowing that the Taihe Temple is completed, the divine images and spirit tablets should be timely enshrined and settled.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day of the second month, an edict declared: "Now that the Taihe Temple is complete, the divine images and spirit tablets should be enshrined and settled without delay.

sentences.zh: 可剋三月三日己巳，內奉遷於正廟。

translations.literal: The third day of the third month, jisi, may be fixed for the inner escort to transfer them to the main temple.
translations.idiomatic: Let the third day of the third month, jisi, be chosen for the inner escort to transfer them to the main temple.

sentences.zh: 其出金墉之儀，一準出代都太和之式。

translations.literal: The ceremony of departing Jinyong should entirely follow the form of departing the Taihe Temple from the capital at Dai.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremony for leaving Jinyong should follow entirely the form used when the Taihe Temple left the capital at Dai.

sentences.zh: 入新廟之典，可依近至金墉之軌。

translations.literal: The rite of entering the new temple may follow the recent track of arriving at Jinyong.
translations.idiomatic: The rite for entering the new temple may follow the recent precedent of arriving at Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 其威儀鹵簿，如出代廟。

translations.literal: Its guard of honor and ceremonial escort should be as when leaving the Dai temple.
translations.idiomatic: Its guard of honor and ceremonial escort should be the same as when leaving the Dai temple.

sentences.zh: 百官奉遷，宜可省之。

translations.literal: The hundred officials escorting the transfer may suitably be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The officials escorting the transfer may suitably be reduced in number.

sentences.zh: 但令朝官四品已上，侍官五品已上及宗室奉迎。」

translations.literal: Only let court officials of the fourth rank and above, attendants of the fifth rank and above, and the imperial clan come to receive them."
translations.idiomatic: Only court officials of the fourth rank and above, attendants of the fifth rank and above, and members of the imperial clan need come to receive them."

sentences.zh: 六月，相州刺史高閭表言：「伏惟太武皇帝發孝思之深誠，同渭陽之遠感，以鄴土舅氏之故鄉，有歸魂之舊宅，故為密皇后立廟於城內，歲時祭祀，置廟戶十家，齋宮三十人。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Gao Lü, Governor of Xiang Province, submitted a memorial saying: "I humbly consider that Emperor Taiwu, moved by the deepest sincerity of filial longing and sharing the distant feeling of Weiyang, because Ye was the old homeland of the maternal clan and there was an old dwelling where the soul returned, therefore established a temple for Empress Mi within the city, with seasonal sacrifices, ten temple households appointed, and thirty persons for the fasting palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Gao Lü, Governor of Xiang Province, submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty's servant reflects that Emperor Taiwu, stirred by the deepest filial devotion and the far-reaching grief of Weiyang, because Ye was the ancestral home of the empress's kin and held the old dwelling to which her soul returned, had a temple built within the city for Empress Mi, with seasonal sacrifices, ten temple households, and thirty attendants for the fasting palace.

sentences.zh: 春秋烝嘗，冠服從事，刺史具威儀，親行薦酌，升降揖讓，與七廟同儀，禮畢，撤會而罷。

translations.literal: In spring and autumn, winter and autumn offerings, with caps and robes attending, the governor fully arrayed the guard of honor and personally performed the offering and libation, ascending and descending with bowing and yielding—the same rites as the seven temples; when the ritual was complete, the assembly was withdrawn and ended.
translations.idiomatic: At the spring and autumn, winter and autumn offerings, all wore ceremonial dress; the governor arrayed the guard of honor, personally performed the offering and libation, and observed the ascending, descending, bowing, and yielding in the same manner as the seven temples; when the rite was finished, the assembly was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 今廟殿虧漏，門牆傾毀，簠簋故敗，行禮有闕。

translations.literal: Now the temple hall leaks and is damaged, the gate and walls lean and collapse, the grain vessels are old and broken, and the performance of the rite has gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Now the temple hall leaks and is in disrepair, the gate and walls are crumbling, the ritual vessels are worn and broken, and the rites can no longer be properly performed.

sentences.zh: 臣備職司，目所親覩。

translations.literal: Your servant, holding this office, has seen it with his own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, in the discharge of his duties, has seen this with his own eyes.

sentences.zh: 若以七廟惟新，明堂初制，配饗之儀，備於京邑者，便應罷壞，輟其常祭。

translations.literal: If because the seven temples are newly renewed and the Bright Hall is first established, and the rites of paired feasting are complete in the capital, this [temple] should then be abolished and its regular sacrifices stopped.
translations.idiomatic: If, because the seven temples have been newly restored and the Bright Hall newly built, and the rites of paired feasting are now complete in the capital, this shrine should be abolished and its regular sacrifices discontinued.

sentences.zh: 如以功高特立，宜應新其靈宇。

translations.literal: If because the merit is lofty and uniquely distinguished, the spirit hall should be renewed.
translations.idiomatic: If, because her merit was lofty and singular, her spirit hall should be rebuilt anew.

sentences.zh: 敢陳所見，伏請恩裁。」

translations.literal: I dare set forth what I have seen; prostrate, I ask your gracious judgment."
translations.idiomatic: I venture to offer my view; I humbly ask Your Majesty to decide."

sentences.zh: 詔罷之。

translations.literal: An edict abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered it discontinued.

sentences.zh: 十一月庚午，帝幸委粟山，議定圓丘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on gengwu, the emperor visited Weisu Mountain to deliberate and fix the round mound.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on gengwu, the emperor went to Weisu Mountain to discuss and establish the round mound rite.

sentences.zh: 己卯，帝在合溫室，引咸陽王禧，司空公穆亮，吏部尚書、任城王澄及議禮之官。

translations.literal: On jimao, the emperor being in He Wen Hall, summoned the Prince of Xianyang, Xi, Director of Works Duke Mu Liang, Minister of Personnel and Prince of Rencheng, Cheng, and the officials who debated ritual.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, at He Wen Hall, the emperor summoned Prince Xi of Xianyang, Director of Works Duke Mu Liang, Prince Cheng of Rencheng—who also held the Ministry of Personnel—and the ritual specialists.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朝集公卿，欲論圓丘之禮。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Morning has gathered the dukes and ministers; I wish to discuss the round mound rite.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ran: "I have summoned the ministers this morning to discuss the round mound rite.

sentences.zh: 今短晷斯極，長日方至。

translations.literal: Now the short shadow has reached its extreme; the long days have just arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The winter solstice is upon us—the shortest shadows have reached their limit, and the days are just beginning to lengthen.

sentences.zh: 案周官祀昊天上帝於圓丘，禮之大者。

translations.literal: Examining the Offices of Zhou: it sacrifices to Haotian Shangdi at the round mound—that is the greatest of rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou prescribe sacrifice to the Supreme God at the round mound—the greatest of all rites.

sentences.zh: 兩漢禮有參差，魏晉猶亦未一。

translations.literal: The rites of the two Han had discrepancies; Wei and Jin too have not yet been uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Even the two Han dynasties observed the rite inconsistently; under Wei and Jin no single standard has prevailed.

sentences.zh: 我魏氏雖上參三皇，下考叔世近代都祭圓丘之禮，復未考周官，為不刊之法令。

translations.literal: Our Wei house, though looking up we consult the Three Sovereigns and looking down we examine the near age and recent times—all sacrifice at the round mound—yet have again not examined the Offices of Zhou into immutable statute.
translations.idiomatic: Our Wei, though tracing precedent to the Three Sovereigns and reviewing recent practice at the round mound, have never grounded these rites in the Offices of Zhou as fixed law.

sentences.zh: 以此祭圓丘之禮示卿等，欲與諸賢考之厥衷。」

translations.literal: With this round mound sacrifice rite I show you ministers; I wish with all worthies to examine its inner meaning."
translations.idiomatic: I present this round-mound ritual for your review and ask you worthy ministers to weigh its true intent."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「夕牲之禮，無可依準，近在代都，已立其議。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The evening-victim rite has nothing to rely on as standard; recently at the capital in Dai we already established deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "For the evening-victim rite there is no reliable precedent. At Dai we recently debated the matter and reached a decision.

sentences.zh: 殺牲祼神，誠是一日之事，終無夕而殺牲，待明而祭。」

translations.literal: Killing victims and libating to the spirits is truly one day's affair; in the end there is never killing victims at evening and waiting for dawn to sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: Slaughter and libation are properly a single day's work—it is unthinkable to kill the victim at dusk and wait until morning to sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 員外散騎常侍劉芳對曰：「臣謹案周官牧人職，正有夕展牲之禮，實無殺牲之事。」

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Extraordinary Liu Fang replied: "Your servant respectfully examines the Offices of Zhou, Herdsman office: properly there is the evening display-victim rite; truly there is no killing-victim matter."
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Extraordinary Liu Fang replied: "Your servant finds in the Herdsman's duties in the Offices of Zhou an evening rite for displaying the victims—but no provision for slaughter at that hour."

sentences.zh: 秘書令李彪曰：「夕不殺牲，誠如聖旨。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Li Biao said: "Not killing victims at evening is truly as the sage edict says.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Li Biao said: "Your Majesty is right not to slaughter victims in the evening.

sentences.zh: 未審告廟以不？

translations.literal: Not yet examined: is announcement to the temple or not?
translations.idiomatic: It is unclear whether one should announce the rite to the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 臣聞魯人將有事于上帝，必先有事于泮宮，注曰，『先人』。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard: when men of Lu were about to have business with Shangdi, they must first have business at the Pan palace; the commentary says, 'forebears.'
translations.idiomatic: I recall that when the people of Lu were to sacrifice to the Lord on High, they first offered at the Pan palace; the commentaries gloss this as honoring their forebears.

sentences.zh: 以此推之，應有告廟。」

translations.literal: By this pushing it, there ought to be announcement to the temple."
translations.idiomatic: By that reasoning, an announcement to the ancestral temple should be required."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿言有理，但朕先以郊配，意欲廢告，而卿引證有據，當從卿議。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words have principle; but I earlier, because the suburban sacrifice has a co-honoree, intended to abolish announcement, yet your citations have basis—I shall follow your deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "You make a fair point. Because our suburban sacrifice pairs with the ancestral co-honoree, I had meant to dispense with the temple announcement—but your citations are well founded. We shall follow your recommendation."

sentences.zh: 帝又曰：「圓丘之牲，色無常準，覽推古事，乖互不一。

translations.literal: The emperor further said: "Round mound victims—color has no fixed standard; viewing and deducing ancient affairs, they are discordant and not one.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor continued: "For round-mound victims, color has no fixed standard. A review of antiquity shows conflicting practices.

sentences.zh: 周家用騂，解言是尚。

translations.literal: The Zhou house used xing; explaining the words, this is what was honored.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou favored reddish-brown victims—the commentaries take this as the preferred color.

sentences.zh: 晉代靡知所據。

translations.literal: The Jin age had none who knew what to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin no one could say what precedent they followed.

sentences.zh: 舜之命禹，悉用堯辭，復言玄牡告于后帝。

translations.literal: When Shun commanded Yu, he altogether used Yao's words, again saying dark bull announcing to the Later Lord.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun charged Yu, he adopted Yao's wording entirely, declaring a dark bull offered to the Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 今我國家，時用夏正，至於牲色，未知何準？」

translations.literal: Now our state and house, the times use the Xia calendar; as for victim color—who knows what standard?"
translations.idiomatic: Our realm keeps the Xia calendar—yet for the color of victims, what standard should we follow?"

sentences.zh: 秘書令李彪曰：「觀古用玄，似取天玄之義，臣謂宜用玄。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Li Biao said: "Observing antiquity's use of xuan, it seems to take the meaning of Heaven's xuan; your servant says one should use xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Biao replied: "Ancient usage favors dark victims, evoking Heaven's own hue. I recommend black.

sentences.zh: 至於五帝，各象其方色，亦有其義。」

translations.literal: As for the Five Emperors, each images his directional color—this too has its meaning."
translations.idiomatic: For the Five Directional Emperors, each color matches its quarter—that too has ritual logic."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「天何時不玄，地何時不黃，意欲從玄。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When is Heaven not xuan? When is Earth not yellow? My intent is to follow xuan."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Is Heaven ever not dark? Is Earth ever not yellow? I mean to follow the darker color."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「我國家常聲鼓以集眾。

translations.literal: He further said: "Our state and house always sound drums to gather the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Our court customarily beats drums to assemble the officials.

sentences.zh: 易稱二至之日，商旅不行，后不省方，以助微陽、微陰。

translations.literal: The Changes says: on the days of the two solstices, traveling merchants do not go, the empress does not inspect the regions, to assist faint yang and faint yin.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says that on the solstices merchants cease travel and the empress suspends her regional tours, so as not to disturb the returning yang or yin.

sentences.zh: 今若依舊鳴鼓，得無闕寢鼓之義。」

translations.literal: Now if we follow the old way in sounding drums, would we not lack the meaning of resting the drum?"
translations.idiomatic: If we continue to beat drums as usual, do we not violate the spirit of the solstice drum-rest?"

sentences.zh: 員外郎崔逸曰：「臣案周禮，當祭之日，靁鼓靁鼗，八面而作，猶不妨陽。

translations.literal: Outer Gentleman Cui Yi said: "Your servant examines the Rites of Zhou: on days of sacrifice, thunder-drums and thunder-tambourines, eight faces sounding—still they do not obstruct yang.
translations.idiomatic: Outer Gentleman Cui Yi said: "The Rites of Zhou prescribe thunder-drums and thunder-tambourines on sacrifice days, beaten on all eight sides—yet this does not harm the yang principle.

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂以鼓集眾，無妨古義。」

translations.literal: Your servant privately thinks that using drums to gather the multitude does not obstruct ancient meaning."
translations.idiomatic: I believe beating drums to assemble the court in no way contravenes ancient practice."

sentences.zh: 癸未詔，三公衮冕八章，太常鷩冕六章，用以陪薦。

translations.literal: On guiwei an edict: the Three Dukes, dark robes with eight emblems; the Director of Ceremonies, pheasant robes with six emblems—used to attend the offerings.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei an edict prescribed that the Three Dukes wear dark ceremonial robes with eight emblems and the Director of Ceremonies pheasant-pattern robes with six emblems, to assist in the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 甲申長至，祀昊天於委粟山，大夫祭。〈〉

translations.literal: On jiashen, winter solstice, they sacrificed to Haotian at Weisu Mountain; grand masters performed the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, the winter solstice, sacrifice to the Supreme Heaven was offered at Weisu Mountain, with grandees officiating.

sentences.zh: 二十年，立方澤於河陰，仍遣使者以太牢祭漢光武及明、章三帝陵。

translations.literal: The twentieth year, they established a square pond at Heyin, and still dispatched envoys with the grand victim to sacrifice at the tombs of Han Guangwu and the three emperors Ming and Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year a square pond altar was built at Heyin, and envoys were sent with the grand victim to sacrifice at the tombs of Emperor Guangwu of Han and Emperors Ming and Zhang.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Notes on collating and correcting the text.
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 牲用黝犢 諸本「牲」訛「牡」，今據冊府卷三二下〈〉、

translations.literal: "Victims use dark calves" — in various editions "victims" is written erroneously as "male"; now emended according to Cefu juan 32b,
translations.idiomatic: "Victims: dark calves" — various editions wrongly read "victim" as "male animal"; emended per Cefu, juan 32b,

sentences.zh: 通典卷四二郊天上後魏道武帝條改。

translations.literal: and Tongdian juan 42, entry on suburban Heaven under Later Wei Emperor Daowu, emended.
translations.idiomatic: with further correction according to Tongdian juan 42, entry on the suburban Heaven rite under Emperor Daowu of Later Wei.

sentences.zh: 牲共用玄牡一 諸本「牡」訛「牲」，今據冊府〈〉

translations.literal: "Victims together use one dark bull" — in various editions "bull" is written erroneously as "victim"; now according to Cefu.
translations.idiomatic: "Shared victims: one dark bull" — various editions wrongly read "bull" as "victim"; emended per Cefu.

sentences.zh: 改。

translations.literal: Emended.
translations.idiomatic: —emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 用馬薦各一 冊府〈〉

translations.literal: "Use horse and jian, one each" — Cefu.
translations.idiomatic: "One horse and one jian offering each" — per Cefu.

translations.literal: "Jian" is written as "deer."
translations.idiomatic: Cefu reads "jian" as "deer."

sentences.zh: 按既云「各一」，應是二物，疑作「鹿」是，但他處不見祭祀用鹿，今不改。

translations.literal: Examining: since it says "one each," there ought to be two things; suspecting "deer" is correct, but elsewhere one does not see deer used in sacrifice—now not emended.
translations.idiomatic: Since the text says "one each," two distinct victims are implied; "deer" may well be correct, but deer appear nowhere else in these sacrificial records, so the original is left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 帝拜后肅拜 諸本「后」作「若」，冊府卷三二下〈〉

translations.literal: "The emperor bowed; the empress performed a respectful bow" — in various editions "empress" reads "ruo"; Cefu juan 32b.
translations.idiomatic: "The emperor bowed and the empress performed a respectful bow" — various editions misread "empress" as "ruo"; Cefu juan 32b.

sentences.zh: 作「后」。

translations.literal: Reads "empress."
translations.idiomatic: Reads "empress."

sentences.zh: 按通典卷四二也作「后」。

translations.literal: Examining: Tongdian juan 42 also has "empress."
translations.idiomatic: Tongdian juan 42 likewise reads "empress."

sentences.zh: 上云：「后率六宮從黑門入」，則后亦參與祭祀，「若」字形近而訛，今據改。

translations.literal: Above it says: "The empress led the Six Palaces in through the Black Gate"—then the empress also participated in sacrifice; "ruo" is near in form and erroneous—now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The passage above states that "the empress led the Six Palaces in through the Black Gate," so the empress did take part in the rite; "ruo" is a graphic error for "empress," and the text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 若有水旱則禱之 諸本「若」訛「各」，今據冊府〈〉

translations.literal: "If there is flood or drought then pray there" — various editions "if" erroneous as "each"; now according to Cefu.
translations.idiomatic: "In cases of flood or drought, prayers were offered there" — various editions wrongly read "if" as "each"; emended per Cefu.

sentences.zh: 改。

translations.literal: Emended.
translations.idiomatic: —emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 幸洛陽 冊府〈〉

translations.literal: "Visited Luoyang" — Cefu.
translations.idiomatic: "Visited Luoyang" — per Cefu.

sentences.zh: 「幸洛陽」上有「四月」二字。

translations.literal: Above "visited Luoyang" are the two characters "fourth month."
translations.idiomatic: Cefu inserts the words "fourth month" before "visited Luoyang."

sentences.zh: 按事見卷三太宗紀泰常八年四月，此條前後都記月，不應獨缺，當脫「四月」二字。

translations.literal: Examining: the affair is seen in Annals juan 3, Taizu, eighth year of Taichang, fourth month; this entry before and after all note month—it should not alone lack—"fourth month" two characters must have dropped out.
translations.idiomatic: The event appears in the Taichang eighth-year, fourth-month entry of Emperor Taizong's annals (juan 3); neighboring entries all give the month, so "fourth month" has clearly dropped out here and should be restored.

sentences.zh: 神䴥二年 冊府〈〉

translations.literal: Second year of Shenjuan — Cefu.
translations.idiomatic: Second year of Shenjuan — per Cefu.

sentences.zh: 上有「太武」二字。

translations.literal: Above are the two characters "Taizu Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Cefu prefixes "Emperor Wu of Taizu."

sentences.zh: 按志例凡始見於志的某帝，在年號上必加廟號，這裏上當有「世祖」二字，傳本脫去。

translations.literal: Examining: by treatise convention, whenever an emperor first appears in the treatise, on the era name one must add the temple name; here above there ought to be "Shizu" two characters—the transmitted text dropped them.
translations.idiomatic: By the treatise's convention, an emperor's first appearance must include his temple name before the era; "Shizu" (Emperor Shizu) is missing here and has dropped from the transmitted text.

sentences.zh: 冊府例改廟號為諡號。

translations.literal: Cefu by convention changes temple names to posthumous names.
translations.idiomatic: Cefu regularly substitutes posthumous titles for temple names.

sentences.zh: 立廟於恒岳華岳嵩岳上 諸本「華」下脫「岳」字，今據冊府〈〉

translations.literal: "Established temples on Mount Heng, Mount Hua, and Mount Song" — in various editions below "Hua" the "peak" character is missing; now according to Cefu.
translations.idiomatic: "Temples were established on Mount Heng, Mount Hua, and Mount Song" — various editions omit "peak" after "Hua"; emended per Cefu.

sentences.zh: 補。

translations.literal: Supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: —supplied.

sentences.zh: 文成皇帝即位二年正月遣有司詣華岳修廟立碑 諸本「二年」作「三年」。

translations.literal: Emperor Wencheng at accession, second year first month, dispatched the relevant officials to Mount Hua to repair the temple and erect a stele — various editions "second year" reads "third year."
translations.idiomatic: "In the first month of the second year of Emperor Wencheng's reign, officials were sent to Mount Hua to repair the temple and erect a stele" — various editions read "third year" for "second year."

sentences.zh: 冊府卷二六〈〉

translations.literal: Cefu juan 26.
translations.idiomatic: Cefu, juan 26.

sentences.zh: 作「二年」，卷三二下〈〉

translations.literal: Reads "second year," juan 32b.
translations.idiomatic: Reads "second year"; Cefu juan 32b.

sentences.zh: 作「興光元年正月」。

translations.literal: Reads "first month, first year of Xingguang."
translations.idiomatic: Reads "first month of the first year of Xingguang."

sentences.zh: 按拓跋濬於拓跋燾的正平二年十月即位，即在本月改元興安，興安只二年，次年改元興光，興光也只二年。

translations.literal: Examining: Tuoba Jun at Tuoba Tao's second year of Zhengping, tenth month acceded; immediately that month changed era to Xing'an; Xing'an only two years; next year changed era to Xingguang; Xingguang also only two years.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Jun succeeded Tuoba Tao in the tenth month of Zhengping 2 and immediately declared the Xing'an era; Xing'an lasted two years, followed by Xingguang, which also lasted two years.

sentences.zh: 這裏「三」字必誤。

translations.literal: Here the character "three" must be erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: The reading "three" here must be wrong.

sentences.zh: 觀上稱「文成皇帝即位」，當是即位後不久事。

translations.literal: Observing above it says "Emperor Wencheng at accession" — it ought to be shortly after accession.
translations.idiomatic: The phrase "upon Emperor Wencheng's accession" indicates a date soon after he took the throne.

sentences.zh: 興安二年正月實在即位後第三個月，今據冊府卷二六改。

translations.literal: Xing'an second year first month is in fact the third month after accession; now emended according to Cefu juan 26.
translations.idiomatic: The first month of Xing'an 2 falls only three months after his accession; emended per Cefu juan 26.

sentences.zh: 冊府卷三二作「興光元年」，恐是以意改。

translations.literal: Cefu juan 32 reads "first year of Xingguang" — I fear this was altered to suit an idea.
translations.idiomatic: Cefu juan 32 gives "first year of Xingguang," perhaps an arbitrary emendation.

sentences.zh: 又魏書例稱廟號，不應此處獨稱「文成皇帝」，上當脫「高宗」二字。

translations.literal: Moreover Wei Shu by convention uses temple names; this place alone should not say "Emperor Wencheng" — above "Gaozong" two characters must have dropped out.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei routinely uses temple names; this lone reference to "Emperor Wencheng" suggests "Gaozong" has dropped out above.

sentences.zh: 聞虛中若有音聲 諸本脫「有」字，今據冊府卷二六〈〉

translations.literal: "If one hears sound within the hollow" — various editions lack the "have" character; now according to Cefu juan 26.
translations.idiomatic: "If sound is heard within the hollow" — various editions omit "have"; emended per Cefu juan 26.

sentences.zh: 補。

translations.literal: Supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: —supplied.

sentences.zh: 十二年閏九月帝親築圓丘於南郊 諸本「閏九月」作「十月」，冊府卷三二〈〉

translations.literal: Twelfth year, intercalary ninth month, the emperor personally built the round mound at the Southern Suburb — various editions "intercalary ninth month" reads "tenth month"; Cefu juan 32.
translations.idiomatic: "In the intercalary ninth month of the twelfth year the emperor personally built the round mound at the Southern Suburb" — various editions read "tenth month" for "intercalary ninth month"; Cefu juan 32.

sentences.zh: 作「閏九月甲子」。

translations.literal: Reads "intercalary ninth month, jiazi."
translations.idiomatic: Reads "jiazi, intercalary ninth month."

sentences.zh: 按卷七下高祖紀作「閏月甲子」。

translations.literal: Examining: Annals juan 7b, Gaozu, reads "intercalary month, jiazi."
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozu annals (juan 7b) give "jiazi, intercalary month."

sentences.zh: 是年魏閏九月，丁未朔，甲子是十八日，十月丁丑朔，無甲子。

translations.literal: That year Wei had intercalary ninth month; dingwei was new moon; jiazi was the eighteenth day; tenth month dingchou new moon—no jiazi.
translations.idiomatic: That year had an intercalary ninth month: dingwei was the new moon, and jiazi fell on the eighteenth day; the tenth month began on dingchou, so no jiazi occurred there.

sentences.zh: 這裏「十月」顯誤，今據紀及冊府改。

translations.literal: Here "tenth month" is clearly erroneous; now emended according to the annals and Cefu.
translations.idiomatic: "Tenth month" here is clearly wrong; emended per the annals and Cefu.

sentences.zh: 志例只記年月，其一月不止一事者始記日。

translations.literal: By treatise convention only year and month are recorded; only when one month has more than one affair does one record the day.
translations.idiomatic: The treatise normally records only year and month; a day is given only when more than one event falls in the same month.

sentences.zh: 冊府「甲子」疑據紀增，今不補。

translations.literal: Cefu's "jiazi" is suspected added from the annals; now not supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: Cefu's "jiazi" was probably added from the annals; it is not supplied here.

sentences.zh: 周改禘為礿 諸本「礿」作「祠」，冊府卷五八０〈〉

translations.literal: "Zhou changed di to yue" — in various editions "yue" is written as "ci"; Cefu juan 580.
translations.idiomatic: "Zhou renamed the summer sacrifice yue" — various editions wrongly read "yue" as "ci"; Cefu juan 580.

sentences.zh: 作「礿」。

translations.literal: Reads "yue."
translations.idiomatic: Reads "yue."

sentences.zh: 按禮記王制「天子犆礿、祫禘、祫嘗、祫烝」，鄭注：「周改夏祭曰礿。」

translations.literal: Examining Record of Rites, Royal Regulations: "The Son of Heaven zhi yue, xia di, xia chang, xia zheng" — Zheng's commentary: "Zhou changed the Xia sacrifice to yue."
translations.idiomatic: The Royal Regulations in the Record of Rites reads: "The Son of Heaven performs zhi yue, xia di, xia chang, and xia zheng." Zheng Xuan comments: "Zhou renamed the summer sacrifice yue."

sentences.zh: 「祠」乃「礿」形近而訛，今據改。

translations.literal: "Ci" is near in form to "yue" and erroneous—now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: "Ci" is a graphic error for "yue," and the text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 祭義稱春禘秋嘗 諸本「禘」作「祭」，冊府〈〉

translations.literal: "Meaning of Sacrifice" says spring di, autumn chang — various editions "di" reads "sacrifice"; Cefu.
translations.idiomatic: The Meaning of Sacrifice reads "spring di, autumn chang" — various editions misread "di" as "sacrifice"; Cefu.

sentences.zh: 作「禘」。

translations.literal: Reads "di."
translations.idiomatic: Reads "di."

sentences.zh: 按禮記祭義作「禘」，「祭」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: Examining: Record of Rites, Meaning of Sacrifice, has "di"; the "sacrifice" character is erroneous—now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The Meaning of Sacrifice in the Record of Rites reads "di"; "sacrifice" is a scribal error, and the text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 依禮春廢犆礿於嘗於蒸則祫不於三時皆行禘祫之禮 冊府卷五八０〈〉

translations.literal: "According to ritual, in spring abolish zhi yue; at chang and at zheng then xia is not at all three seasons all perform di-xia rite" — Cefu juan 580.
translations.idiomatic: "By ritual, spring omits the zhi yue; at chang and zheng the xia rite is not performed in all three seasons alike" — Cefu juan 580.

sentences.zh: 作「依禮：春廢祫，犆礿，於禘則禘祫，嘗則禘嘗，於烝則祫烝，不廢三時，三時皆行禘祫之禮」。

translations.literal: Reads "According to ritual: in spring abolish xia, zhi yue; at di then di-xia, at chang then di-chang, at zheng then xia-zheng; do not abolish the three seasons—the three seasons all perform the di-xia rite."
translations.idiomatic: Reads: "By ritual, spring omits xia and performs zhi yue; at di, di and xia together; at chang, di and chang together; at zheng, xia and zheng together; the three seasons are not abolished, and all three perform the di-xia rite."

sentences.zh: 通典卷五０祫禘下載此議作「依禮，春廢特礿，於嘗於烝則祫嘗祫烝，不於三時皆行禘祫之禮」。

translations.literal: Tongdian juan 50, Xia-Di section, records this discussion as "According to ritual, in spring abolish te yue; at chang and at zheng then xia-chang xia-zheng; not at all three seasons all perform di-xia rite."
translations.idiomatic: Tongdian, juan 50, under Xia and Di, records this deliberation as: "By ritual, spring omits the special yue; at chang and zheng, xia-chang and xia-zheng; the di-xia rite is not performed in all three seasons alike."

sentences.zh: 按禮記王制：「天子犆礿、祫禘、祫嘗、祫烝。」

translations.literal: Examining Record of Rites, Royal Regulations: "The Son of Heaven zhi yue, xia di, xia chang, xia zheng."
translations.idiomatic: The Royal Regulations in the Record of Rites reads: "The Son of Heaven performs zhi yue, xia di, xia chang, and xia zheng."

sentences.zh: 鄭注：「犆猶一也，祫合也。〈〉

translations.literal: Zheng's commentary: "Zhi means 'only one'; xia means 'join together.'
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan comments: "Zhi means 'only one'; xia means 'joining together.'

sentences.zh: 凡祫之歲，春一礿而已，不祫，以物無成者，不殷祭。」

translations.literal: In every year of xia, spring has only one yue, no xia, because things have not matured—no grand sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: In every year when xia is performed, spring has only a single yue and no xia, because the harvest is not yet ripe and no grand sacrifice is held."

sentences.zh: 則四時之祭，唯春不祫，其餘三時之祭，禘、嘗、烝都祫。

translations.literal: Thus the four-season sacrifices: only spring does not xia; the other three seasons' sacrifices—di, chang, zheng—all xia.
translations.idiomatic: Thus among the four seasonal sacrifices, only spring omits xia; di, chang, and zheng in the other three seasons all include xia.

sentences.zh: 這裏文有訛脫，「廢」下當從冊府有「祫」字，即鄭注「春一礿而已，不合」之意。

translations.literal: Here the text is corrupt and deficient; after "abolish" there should be "xia" per Cefu—the sense of Zheng's note "spring has only one yue, no joining."
translations.idiomatic: Here the text is corrupt and incomplete; after "abolish" Cefu supplies "xia," matching Zheng's meaning that in spring there is only one yue and no joining.

sentences.zh: 下文只說嘗、烝，不及夏祭之禘，則四時缺一，也當從冊府有「於禘則祫禘」〈〉

translations.literal: The text below mentions only chang and zheng, not the summer di sacrifice—then one of the four seasons is missing; per Cefu there should also be "at di then xia di"
translations.idiomatic: The passage below mentions only chang and zheng, not the summer di sacrifice, leaving one of the four seasons unaccounted for; Cefu also has "at di, then xia di"

sentences.zh: 一句。

translations.literal: —one sentence.
translations.idiomatic: —one sentence.

sentences.zh: 最後一句「不於三時皆行禘祫之禮」，和王制本文不合，「不於」二字乃「不廢三時」之訛脫。

translations.literal: The final sentence "not at all three seasons all perform di-xia rite" does not match the Royal Regulations text; "not at all" is a corruption of "do not abolish the three seasons."
translations.idiomatic: The final line, "the di-xia rite is not performed in all three seasons alike," does not match the Royal Regulations; "not at all" is a corruption of "do not abolish the three seasons."

sentences.zh: 前云「廢」，後云「不廢」，前後相應。

translations.literal: Earlier it says "abolish," later "do not abolish"—the two correspond.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the text says "abolish," later "do not abolish"—the two readings correspond.

sentences.zh: 疑原文當作「依禮：春廢祫，犆礿，於禘則祫禘，於嘗、於烝則祫嘗祫烝，不廢三時，三時皆行禘祫之禮」。

translations.literal: Suspect the original should read "According to ritual: in spring abolish xia, zhi yue; at di then xia di; at chang and at zheng then xia chang xia zheng; do not abolish the three seasons—the three seasons all perform the di-xia rite."
translations.idiomatic: The original text probably read: "By ritual, spring omits xia and performs zhi yue; at di, xia di; at chang and zheng, xia chang and xia zheng; the three seasons are not abolished, and all three perform the di-xia rite."

sentences.zh: 通典訛脫與此志略同，不可解。

translations.literal: Tongdian's corruption and omission are roughly the same as this treatise's—inexplicable.
translations.idiomatic: Tongdian's corruptions and omissions closely match those in this treatise and are equally inexplicable.

sentences.zh: 論稱禘自既灌事似據 按語未足，下當有脫文。

translations.literal: "Discussion" reads "di from after the libation shi si ju" — Comment: the statement is insufficient; there must be omitted text below.
translations.idiomatic: The passage reads "di from after the libation" followed by the corrupt characters "shi si ju" — the wording is incomplete, and text must be missing below.

sentences.zh: 通典卷五０「禘自既灌」下有「以往」二字，無「事似據」三字。

translations.literal: Tongdian juan 50, under "di from after the libation," has the two characters "and onward"; it lacks the three characters "shi si ju."
translations.idiomatic: Tongdian, juan 50, after "di from after the libation" has the two characters "and onward," without the three corrupt characters "shi si ju."

sentences.zh: 通典錄文本有節略，「以往」二字乃據論語增，此志原文不必同通典，今於「據」下句斷。

translations.literal: Tongdian's recorded text is abbreviated; "and onward" was added from the Analects; this treatise's original need not match Tongdian—now break the sentence after "ju."
translations.idiomatic: Tongdian's text is abbreviated, and "and onward" was supplied from the Analects; the original of this treatise need not match Tongdian, so the sentence break is placed after "ju."

sentences.zh: 高閭曰 按這是關於祭祀六宗之議，上未叙明，乍觀不知高閭所議何事。

translations.literal: Gao Lu said — Comment: this is discussion on sacrifice to the Six Honored Ones; the passage above does not explain it; at first glance one cannot tell what Gao Lu is debating.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu said — Comment: this concerns deliberation on sacrifice to the Six Honored Ones; the passage above gives no context, and at first reading one cannot tell what Gao Lu is discussing.

sentences.zh: 通典卷四四注引此節，上有「時大議禋祀之禮」七字，始接「高閭曰」，知上必有脫文。

translations.literal: Tongdian juan 44 note quotes this passage; above it are seven characters "At the time there was great debate on the di-worship rite," then connecting to "Gao Lu said"—know that above there must be omitted text.
translations.idiomatic: A note in Tongdian, juan 44, quotes this passage with seven characters above it—"At the time there was great debate on the di-worship rite"—before "Gao Lu said," showing that text must be missing above.

sentences.zh: 高閭議有云「比較臣等評議取衷，附之祀典」，似當有元宏命羣臣議六宗語，所脫或不止通典所有的七字。

translations.literal: Gao Lu's discussion says "Compare our ministers' deliberations and choose the middle course, attach to the sacrificial canon"—seems there should be language of Yuan Hong ordering ministers to discuss the Six Honored Ones; the omission may be more than Tongdian's seven characters.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu's deliberation includes the phrase "Compare our ministers' deliberations and choose the middle course, attach it to the sacrificial canon"—suggesting there should be a passage in which Yuan Hong ordered the ministers to debate the Six Honored Ones, and the omission may exceed Tongdian's seven characters.

sentences.zh: 丘澤初志 冊府卷四〈〉

translations.literal: "Original intent of mound and marsh sacrifice" — Cefu juan 4.
translations.idiomatic: "Original intent of mound and marsh sacrifice" — Cefu, juan 4.

sentences.zh: 「志」作「制」，疑是。

translations.literal: Reads "zhi" as "regulations"—probably correct.
translations.idiomatic: Reads "zhi" as "regulations"—probably correct.

sentences.zh: 若棄秦則中原有寄 按高閭主張以魏承苻秦，此語與閭本意不合，「棄」當是「承」或「繼」之訛，也可能「有」為「無」之訛。

translations.literal: "If one abandons Qin then the Central Plains has a refuge" — Comment: Gao Lu held that Wei succeeded Former Qin; this phrase does not match Lu's intent; "abandon" should be "inherit" or "succeed," or possibly "has" is a corruption for "has not."
translations.idiomatic: "If one abandons Qin, the Central Plains has a refuge" — Comment: Gao Lu argued that Wei succeeded Fu Jian's Qin, so this wording contradicts his intent; "abandon" is probably a corruption for "inherit" or "succeed," and "has" may be a corruption for "has not."

sentences.zh: 平文太祖抗衡苻石終平燕氏 按此「太祖」乃指拓跋珪，故云「終平燕氏」，下穆亮等議引述李彪原議稱「始自平文，逮於太祖，抗衡燕趙，終平慕容」，平文和太祖分述，意更明白。

translations.literal: "Emperors Wen and Taizu stood against Fu Jian and Shi Hu, finally conquered the Murong Yan" — Comment: here "Taizu" refers to Tuoba Gui, hence "finally conquered the Murong Yan"; below Mu Liang and others quote Li Biao's original discussion: "From Emperor Wen through Emperor Taizu, stood against Yan and Zhao, finally overthrew the Murong"—separating Wen and Taizu makes the meaning clearer.
translations.idiomatic: "Emperors Wen and Taizu stood against Fu Jian and Shi Hu and finally conquered the Murong Yan" — Comment: here "Taizu" refers to Tuoba Gui, hence "finally conquered the Murong Yan"; below, Mu Liang and others quote Li Biao's original argument: "From Emperor Wen through Emperor Taizu, they stood against Yan and Zhao and finally overthrew the Murong"—distinguishing Wen and Taizu makes the sense clearer.

sentences.zh: 但此時「太祖」即平文帝廟號，下文明云「平文始大，廟號太祖」，拓跋珪廟號是烈祖，至次年四月始改珪廟號「太祖」，豈得先有此稱？

translations.literal: But at this time "Taizu" was Emperor Wen's temple name; the text below clearly says "Wen first grew great, temple name Taizu"; Tuoba Gui's temple name was Liezu—only in the fourth month of the following year was Gui's temple name changed to "Taizu"—how could this title appear earlier?
translations.idiomatic: But at this point "Taizu" was already Emperor Wen's temple name; the passage below explicitly says "Wen first grew great, and his temple name was Taizu," whereas Tuoba Gui's temple name was Liezu and was not changed to "Taizu" until the fourth month of the following year—so how could the title appear here first?

sentences.zh: 疑本作「烈祖」，後人所改。

translations.literal: Suspect the original read "Liezu"—altered by later hands.
translations.idiomatic: The original probably read "Liezu" and was altered by a later copyist.

sentences.zh: 新泰侯游明根 諸本「泰」作「秦」。

translations.literal: Marquis of Xintai You Minggen — various editions read "Tai" as "Qin."
translations.idiomatic: You Minggen, Marquis of Xintai — various editions misread "Tai" as "Qin."

sentences.zh: 洪氏考異卷一０云：「『新秦』當作『新泰』。

translations.literal: Hong's Critical Notes, juan 10, states: "'Xin Qin' should read 'Xin Tai.'
translations.idiomatic: Hong Yixuan's Critical Notes, juan 10, states: "'Xin Qin' should read 'Xin Tai.'

sentences.zh: 游明根傳〈〉

translations.literal: Biography of You Minggen
translations.idiomatic: Biography of You Minggen

sentences.zh: 『就拜東兗州刺史，改爵新泰侯』。」

translations.literal: 'He was immediately appointed Inspector of Eastern Yan Province and ennobled Marquis of Xintai.'
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately appointed Inspector of Eastern Yan Province and ennobled Marquis of Xintai."

sentences.zh: 按新泰屬北徐州東泰山郡，「新秦」，北魏不聞有此縣，洪說是，今改正。

translations.literal: Examining: Xintai belonged to Eastern Mount Tai commandery in Northern Xu Province; "Xin Qin"—Northern Wei had no such county; Hong's view is correct—now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Xintai belonged to Eastern Mount Tai commandery in Northern Xu Province; "Xin Qin" is unknown in Northern Wei records; Hong is correct, and the text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 已於中省 按下文稱策諡孔丘，「帝齋於中書省」，當時洛陽孔廟即在中書省，這裏「中省」下當脫「置」字。

translations.literal: "Already at the Central Secretariat" — Comment: below it says the edict conferring posthumous honors on Confucius, "the Emperor fasted at the Secretariat"; at the time Luoyang's Confucius temple was within the Secretariat—here after "Central Secretariat" the character "establish" is missing.
translations.idiomatic: "Already at the Central Secretariat" — Comment: the passage below on conferring a posthumous title on Confucius reads "the Emperor fasted at the Secretariat," and Luoyang's Confucius temple was then located within the Secretariat; the character "establish" is missing after "Central Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 故太祖有三層之宇已降無方丈之室 諸本「已降」作「巴陵」，通典卷四七太和十六年十月條作「已降」。

translations.literal: "Former Taizu had three-tier halls; from him down none had one-square-room halls" — various editions read "from him down" as "Baling"; Tongdian juan 47, entry for tenth month of Taihe 16, reads "from him down."
translations.idiomatic: "Former Taizu had halls of three tiers; from him down there were no one-square-room halls" — various editions misread "from him down" as "Baling"; Tongdian, juan 47, under the tenth month of Taihe 16, reads "from him down."

sentences.zh: 按元宏以前北魏諸帝並無曾封「巴陵」者。

translations.literal: Examining: before Yuan Hong no Northern Wei emperor had ever been enfeoffed as "Marquis of Baling."
translations.idiomatic: Before Yuan Hong, no Northern Wei emperor had ever held the title "Marquis of Baling."

sentences.zh: 「巴陵」乃「已降」之訛，指拓跋嗣已下諸帝，下云「自太宗諸帝，昔無殿宇」可證，今據改。

translations.literal: "Baling" is a corruption of "from him down," referring to emperors from Tuoba Si down; below it says "from Emperor Taizong on, formerly no hall buildings"—can verify—now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: "Baling" is a corruption of "from him down," referring to emperors from Tuoba Si onward; the passage below, "from Emperor Taizong on, formerly no hall buildings," confirms this, and the text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 二月癸亥詔曰知太和廟已就〈〉

translations.literal: On guihai of the second month an edict said: knowing the Taihe Temple is complete
translations.idiomatic: On guihai of the second month an edict said that the Taihe Temple was complete

sentences.zh: 可剋三月三日己巳內奉遷於正廟 諸本「二月」作「三月」，通典卷四七作「二月」，又「三月三日己巳」，通典作「五月」。

translations.literal: Can set the third month third day jisi to move [tablets] within to the main temple — various editions read "second month" as "third month"; Tongdian juan 47 reads "second month"; and for "third month third day jisi," Tongdian reads "fifth month."
translations.idiomatic: The tablets may be moved into the main temple on the third day, jisi, of the third month — various editions misread "second month" as "third month"; Tongdian, juan 47, reads "second month," and for "third month, third day, jisi" it reads "fifth month."

sentences.zh: 按太和十九年三月庚午朔，無「癸亥」，二月庚子朔，「癸亥」乃二十五日。

translations.literal: Examining: in Taihe 19, third month gengwu new moon—no "guihai"; second month gengzi new moon—"guihai" is the twenty-fifth day.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 19 the third month began on gengwu, so there was no "guihai"; the second month began on gengzi, and "guihai" fell on the twenty-fifth day.

sentences.zh: 卷七下高祖紀下太和十九年二月戊辰：「行幸碻磝。

translations.literal: Annals juan 7b, Gaozu B, Taihe 19 second month wuchen: "The Emperor traveled to Qiaodao.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozu annals (juan 7b) for Taihe 19, second month, wuchen, read: "The Emperor traveled to Qiaodao.

sentences.zh: 太和廟成。」

translations.literal: The Taihe Temple was completed."
translations.idiomatic: The Taihe Temple was completed."

sentences.zh: 戊辰乃三十日，當是不知確在哪一日，故系於月盡，其廟成實在二月癸亥前。

translations.literal: Wuchen is the thirtieth day—probably because the exact day was unknown, so it was placed at month's end; the temple was actually completed before guihai of the second month.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchen is the thirtieth day—the date was probably uncertain, so the entry was placed at month's end; the temple was in fact completed before guihai of the second month.

sentences.zh: 這裏「三月」乃「二月」之訛，今據改。

translations.literal: Here "third month" is a corruption of "second month"—now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Here "third month" is a corruption of "second month," and the text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 又三月亦無「己巳」，五月己巳朔，非三日。

translations.literal: Moreover the third month also has no "jisi"; fifth month jisi new moon—not the third day.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the third month has no "jisi"; in the fifth month "jisi" is the new-moon day, not the third day.

sentences.zh: 卷七下高祖紀下是年五月庚午〈〉

translations.literal: Annals juan 7b, Gaozu B, that year fifth month gengwu
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozu annals (juan 7b) for that year, fifth month, gengwu

sentences.zh: 「遷文成皇后馮氏神主於太和廟」。

translations.literal: "Moved the spirit tablet of Empress Wen Cheng, née Feng, to the Taihe Temple."
translations.idiomatic: "Moved the spirit tablet of Empress Wen Cheng, née Feng, to the Taihe Temple."

sentences.zh: 疑「三月三日己巳」為「五月朔日己巳」之訛。

translations.literal: Suspect "third month third day jisi" is a corruption of "fifth month new-moon day jisi."
translations.idiomatic: "Third month, third day, jisi" is probably a corruption of "fifth month, new-moon day, jisi."

sentences.zh: 但此志所云所遷者似指歷代神主，紀唯云遷馮太后神主，又差一日，不知何故。

translations.literal: But what this treatise says was moved seems to refer to spirit tablets of successive generations; the annals mention only moving Empress Dowager Feng's tablet—and differ by one day; the reason is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: But the tablets said to have been moved here seem to mean those of successive generations, whereas the annals mention only Empress Dowager Feng's tablet—and the dates differ by one day; the reason is unclear.
